Title: Matcha in food: Healthy innovation or marketing gimmick?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Matcha, a powdered Japanese green tea that once dominated the beverage scene, particularly at trendy cafes, before making its way to roadside stalls, is now gaining wider popularity in the culinary industry.
No longer confined to lattes, fancy drinks and desserts, matcha is increasingly being incorporated into a variety of savoury dishes, including nasi lemak, burgers and even fried catfish.
While such combinations may sound unusual, they have found their own following, with some consumers embracing the notion that 'the greener, the healthier'.
But does this growing trend of matcha-infused dishes represent creative culinary innovation and a healthier way of eating, or is it simply a marketing strategy to attract attention and gain popularity on social media?
Innovation or health eating?
Senior lecturer at the Department of Science and Mathematics, Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia, Dr Adnin Afifi Nawi, views the current phenomenon primarily as a form of culinary creativity aimed at attracting customers.
He said that although matcha has antioxidant properties, various factors must be considered before labelling matcha-containing dishes as 'healthy' options.
"If a food item goes viral because of its attractive colour or unique taste, there is nothing wrong with giving it a try. However, we should not immediately conclude that it is healthy simply because it contains matcha," he told Bernama.
Noting that consumer preferences have evolved, he said uniqueness and visual appeal, particularly when shared on social media, had become priorities among young people.
"In the past, we chose food based on taste and quality, but purchasing behaviour has changed. Today, being 'unique' and 'beautiful' enough to post on TikTok or Instagram has become a priority. In the digital economy, consumer attention is a goldmine.
"The more unusual or extraordinary a dish is, the greater its potential to be shared and go viral.
"Matcha's vibrant green colour makes it highly photogenic. If a food picture or video manages to captivate netizens within the first three seconds, the dish is likely to become highly sought after," he said.
He added that international media had reported the growing global popularity of matcha, with demand for the ingredient outstripping supply.
"Reports by the South China Morning Post have also revealed that some traditional producers in Japan are struggling to meet surging global demand, fuelled by the influence of social media," he said.
[[nid:1560283]]
Understanding matcha
Explaining the health benefits of matcha from a scientific perspective, Professor Dr Norsham Juliana Nordin, an expert in chronophysiology and chrononutrition at the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia, said matcha is a powdered green tea derived from the Camellia sinensis plant and contains catechins, which are potent antioxidants.
Consuming foods containing catechins may help reduce inflammation in the body, boost metabolism, support weight management, and promote heart and blood vessel health. Matcha also has natural antibacterial and antiviral properties.
However, the nutrition expert stressed that the health value of a dish cannot be determined solely by the presence of a single ingredient considered beneficial.
Instead, she said, a balanced approach to healthy eating requires consideration of the overall composition of a meal, including portion size, preparation methods, frequency of consumption and timing.
"Matcha does have a sound nutritional basis because it contains polyphenols, particularly catechins such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), as well as L-theanine and caffeine. Its use is therefore not merely a gimmick.
"However, when matcha is added to nasi lemak, burgers, noodles, traditional cakes or desserts, we cannot automatically assume that the entire dish has become a 'health food'.
"The nutritional value is still determined by the overall dish. If only a small amount of matcha is added while the food remains high in calories, sugar, saturated fat or sodium, the overall nutritional impact does not change dramatically," she told Bernama.
Matcha nasi lemak and fried catfish
On viral food creations such as matcha nasi lemak and matcha-marinated fried catfish, Norsham Juliana said matcha had strong sensory appeal, with its green colour, umami flavour and slight bitterness lending dishes a premium image.
However, adding the ingredient to nasi lemak or fried catfish does not necessarily make either dish healthier.
"For nasi lemak, the calorie, fat and sodium content, as well as portion size, still depend on the amount of coconut milk, sambal, anchovies and oil used, and how much is consumed. Adding matcha to the rice may contribute some polyphenols and introduce a variation in flavour and colour, but it does not 'neutralise' the coconut milk, salt or excess calories.
[[nid:1560282]]
"A more meaningful way to make nasi lemak more balanced is to control portion size and the amount of coconut milk, oil and sodium used, while adding vegetables or cucumber. Choosing healthier cooking methods for the accompanying dishes would also help. Matcha can then be included as a creative addition.
"In other words, matcha may add value, but it is not a licence to disregard the nutritional composition of the entire meal," she said.
The same applies to catfish prepared using matcha as a marinade.
She said matcha could contribute phenolic compounds, flavour and colour to the fish, but clinical evidence remained insufficient to claim that matcha-marinated catfish offered greater health benefits than conventionally prepared catfish.
"The greater difference to health usually comes from how the fish is cooked. Catfish marinated in matcha but deep-fried in large amounts of oil is still affected by the quantity of oil used, frying temperature, portion size and accompanying sauces.
"By contrast, grilled, baked or roasted fish prepared with controlled amounts of oil and salt generally has a better nutritional profile," she explained.
At the same time, Norsham Juliana cautioned that exposing matcha to excessively high temperatures could reduce some of its beneficial properties.
"Catechins are not immune to heat. A study on matcha-enriched biscuits found that baking reduced the total catechin content by about 19 per cent compared with the dough. A bread study, meanwhile, showed that a substantial proportion of certain catechins could be retained after baking, although EGCG and epigallocatechin (EGC) were more susceptible to degradation than some other catechins," she said.
"More precisely, cooking can reduce or alter some of matcha's bioactive compounds, but it does not necessarily eliminate all of them. The higher the temperature and the longer the exposure, the greater the likelihood of changes occurring," she added.
The risks of too much matcha
While enjoying matcha-infused dishes, consumers should also be aware of the potential risks associated with excessive consumption of foods containing the ingredient.
"Many people assume that 'this cake contains matcha, so it must be healthier', or that 'this drink is green, so I can drink it frequently'. Another common mistake is overlooking the quantity consumed.
"In reality, the benefits and risks depend on the dose. A small serving is not the same as drinking several strong matcha beverages a day in addition to eating matcha desserts," Norsham Juliana explained.
Citing the European Food Safety Authority, she said consuming 800 milligrammes or more of EGCG daily through food supplements had been associated with increased liver enzyme levels.
"High doses or the use of highly concentrated green tea extracts should not be regarded in the same way as ordinary food consumption. Safety assessments indicate that liver injury is rare, but particular attention is given to supplements or concentrated extracts containing high doses of EGCG, especially when taken as a large single dose," she stressed.
She also advised consumers to consider matcha's caffeine content and the timing of consumption, particularly if they were sensitive to caffeine.
"A third common mistake is overlooking timing. From the perspective of chrononutrition and chronophysiology, both what we consume and when we consume it matter. Drinking matcha in the morning has different implications for sleep compared with consuming a caffeinated matcha beverage late at night," she said.
She added that excessive matcha consumption could cause caffeine-sensitive individuals to experience headaches, palpitations, restlessness and difficulty sleeping.
"There is nothing wrong with enjoying matcha, but do not eat with your eyes alone. Its green colour is appealing, but health cannot be judged by colour or a single ingredient.
"If you choose a matcha drink, reduce the amount of sugar and syrup. If you opt for matcha cake or pastries, remember that they are still desserts and keep your portions under control," she advised.
She recommended that consumers practise moderation rather than blindly subscribing to the notion that 'the greener, the healthier'.

Title: Shuhaily: Public support gives me strength to face court proceedings
Article:
SEPANG: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has thanked the public for their prayers and messages of support ahead of his court proceedings today.
He said the encouragement from people across all walks of life meant a great deal to him as he faced the legal process.
"I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to everyone who has supported me and offered prayers and messages of support.
"That is what has given me the strength and confidence to continue with these legal proceedings," he told a brief press conference at the lobby of the Sepang magistrate's court complex this morning.
Shuhaily said he would leave it to the court to conduct the legal proceedings in accordance with due process.
He also said this would be his final press conference concerning the case.
"This is my last press conference regarding these legal proceedings. Once the court proceedings are over, my lawyer will speak on my behalf," he said.
Earlier, Shuhaily, 54,
arrived at the court complex
around 7.30am wearing a suit and was later seen having breakfast at the canteen.
Port Klang MCBA commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal was also present to show his support.
Security was tightened at the court complex, with an increased presence of police and Rela personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Anyone but Trump': Republicans face Latino backlash over immigration raids
Article:
DORAL: For nearly two years, US President Donald Trump's heavy-handed deportation drive has sown fear in immigrant communities and generated a flood of grim headlines and social media videos.
Now, with midterm elections looming, many Latino voters who helped propel Trump and his Republican Party to power in 2024 say they are fed up.
In southern Florida's Doral, a mostly Latino community near Miami that is also home to one of Trump's golf clubs, residents told AFP that fears of potential raids have left businesses short-staffed and classrooms with fewer pupils.
Known as "Doralzuela", the area is home to a large Venezuelan population and could be a bellwether of shifting Latino sentiment nationwide.
"I feel sad and disappointed," restaurant owner Maria Fernanda Perez told AFP.
"My thinking was that the economy would improve," the 32-year-old said of her vote for Trump.
Three of her employees had stopped showing up for work for fear of being deported, she said, while sales had fallen 40 per cent as people in the community cut back on going out.
"My whole family, all my friends are going through immigration proceedings, and they're no longer working, they're no longer going about their daily lives."
Trump campaigned on promises of a historic deportation drive, but emphasised targeting hardened criminals.
With more than 1,000 people being taken into immigration custody every day, many Latino voters feel misled.
Like other communities around the country, residents in Doral have begun exchanging messages to alert one another to the presence of immigration agents or someone being detained.
A New York Times and Siena College poll conducted last month showed that 66 per cent of Hispanic respondents disapproved of Trump's performance, while 78 per cent said they would prefer Democrats to take control of Congress from Republicans.
Perez declined to say how she would vote in the upcoming election, but said emphatically: "Anyone but Trump."
[[nid:1560274]]
Psychological pressure
Carlos Bermudez, a lawyer of Venezuelan origin, receives constant calls from desperate people going through immigration proceedings.
"They don't go out, they can't go to work... It's constant psychological pressure, and it affects the whole community," the 47-year-old told AFP.
Bermudez, who describes himself as a Republican, expressed concern about the party's increasingly "extreme" positions.
"I'm a Republican because I come from a country where communism, socialism took hold, and I don't want to continue with that ideology, but I don't agree with what the extreme wing of the party is doing now," he said.
Doral councilman Rafael Pineyro said he saw the crackdown's impact not only in his city but across southern Florida.
"There's uncertainty, there's fear... It's not just Doral, it's the whole Latino community in South Florida that's affected," he said from his office at city hall.
Pineyro, a Republican, also questioned the Trump administration's immigration strategy.
"This isn't right, because this isn't what was promised in 2024 when we were talking about (deporting) criminals," he said.
Trump's policies could undermine gains made by Republicans in recent years among Florida's Cuban, Venezuelan and other Latino voters, he warned.
"That opportunity has been slipping away more and more in recent months because of bad decisions, in my view, specifically when it comes to the economy and immigration."

Title: Afdlin Shauki recounts five-hour ordeal trapped in Paris riots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Actor and comedian Datuk Afdlin Shauki Aksan was trapped in Paris for five hours amid riots, with his wife and three-year-old daughter.
In a Facebook post, Afdlin said he had travelled to France with his family to attend the International Market of Communications Programmes (Mipcom) in Cannes before spending time in Paris.
Their outing near the Louvre took a frightening turn when they encountered a demonstration.
"We came across a demonstration. Many of the participants were young people. To be fair, many of them were very polite and kind. Not everyone there was looking to cause trouble.
"When people began running in all directions, we were in front of a store. The staff saw us with Inaya, who is only three years old.
"They immediately let us in and locked the door," he said.
Afdlin said the family later left the store when the situation appeared to calm down, but could not find a way out of the area.
"Eventually, we took shelter in a restaurant connected to a nearby hotel."
He said he could not remember the restaurant's name but would always remember the elderly couple who ran it and the other patrons who looked out for his daughter.
Afdlin said the situation worsened when he saw rioters fleeing outside and tear gas seeped into the restaurant.
"My little girl began to panic and struggled to breathe. My wife was hit in the eyes by pepper spray, while I felt some tightness in my chest.
"As a father, seeing your own child frightened and struggling to breathe is incredibly difficult. At that moment, all we wanted was to make sure she was safe," he said.
Despite the ordeal, Afdlin cautioned against judging the whole of France based on incidents in one area.
"I heard reports of incidents elsewhere, including in Nice over the weekend, but I can only speak as a witness to what we experienced ourselves in Paris," he said.
He also urged Malaysians travelling abroad to prioritise their safety.
"Do not wait around to film or see what happens. Find shelter, follow the authorities' instructions and check official information before continuing your journey.
"No tourist attraction is more important than your family's safety. This experience left us frightened, but also deeply grateful," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perlis MB suspended from Bersatu for two terms
Article:
PADANG BESAR: Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah has been suspended from Bersatu for two party election terms, effective Oct 13.
Perlis Bersatu chairman Izizam Ibrahim confirmed the authenticity of a suspension letter dated Oct 14 and signed by Bersatu Disciplinary Board chairman Datuk Mohd Radzi Manan.
Izizam said the letter had been issued last week but denied circulating it.
"Yes, the letter was issued last week, but I was not the one who circulated it. The menteri besar is also aware of the suspension letter.
"For now, we are waiting for an official decision from the Bersatu central leadership and Pas assemblymen," he said.
The letter notifying Abu Bakar of his suspension went viral on social media earlier.
According to the letter, the party's Disciplinary Board, which met on Oct 13, decided to suspend Abu Bakar's membership rights for two party election terms under Clause 22.5.
The action was reportedly taken after he breached Clause 9.1.4 of the party constitution and its Code of Ethics and Conduct.
Following the suspension, Abu Bakar would automatically lose all positions he held in the party and be barred from making statements on its behalf until the suspension period ends.
However, the notice stated that he could appeal to the party's Appeals Board within 14 days of the notice's date.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shuhaily charged with hurting two Special Branch policemen
Article:
SEPANG: Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court to two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to two Special Branch policemen last month.
Shuhaily, 54, was charged with voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman and Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, on Sept 28 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1.
The charges, under Section 323 of the Penal Code, carry a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Shuhaily, who stood near the dock, told magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani that he understood the charges and claimed trial.
He appeared calm during the proceedings.

Title: Iskandar Malaysia hits RM525bil, sets sights on bigger gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia has attracted RM525.26 billion in investments over two decades, exceeding its original RM383 billion target by RM142.26 billion, as Johor's flagship economic corridor shifts towards higher-value industries and deeper cross-border integration to sustain its next phase of growth.
The focus is now on translating investment momentum into higher productivity, better-paying jobs and stronger domestic supply chains, with the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) expected to play a pivotal role in positioning the region as a more competitive regional business and industrial hub.
According to the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA), the corridor has generated more than one million jobs and more than doubled average household incomes since its establishment.
With competition for investments intensifying across Asean, IRDA is shifting its priorities from broad-based expansion towards quality investments that deliver greater economic value, strengthen local businesses and create opportunities for Malaysians to move up the value chain.
The next phase will prioritise advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, modern logistics, and high-value financial and business services, positioning Iskandar Malaysia to capture a greater share of regional and global economic activity.
"For the next development phase, emphasis will be placed on increasing productivity and high-value economic activity, including advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, and logistics, as well as financial and business services," IRDA said in a statement.
The authority said the emphasis would extend beyond the value of investments secured to include technology transfer, domestic business participation, local innovation and the ability of Malaysian companies to move up the global value chain.
At the centre of this strategy is the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), which is expected to strengthen the economic relationship between the two markets by combining Johor's industrial capacity and competitive operating expenses with Singapore's access to international capital, technology and business networks.
The JS-SEZ attracted RM76.98 billion in approved investments in 2025, underscoring Johor's growing appeal as a complementary investment destination for businesses seeking to expand their regional operations.
Deputy Prime Minister II and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the next phase of Iskandar Malaysia's development must be measured by the quality and sustainability of its economic gains, rather than investment figures alone.
Fadillah chaired the 36th IRDA Governing Council meeting on behalf of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, alongside Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
"The next phase should be assessed not only by the total investment attracted but also by the quality of opportunities created, the strength of the economic ecosystem, and the long-term benefits that businesses and communities can enjoy," he said.
IRDA said land availability and competitive costs, once major considerations for investors, were no longer sufficient to secure a competitive advantage as businesses increasingly assessed the readiness of infrastructure, reliability of energy supply, availability of skilled workers and quality of digital connectivity.
The efficiency of cross-border movement for goods and people, as well as access to regional and international markets, has also become increasingly important in investment decisions.
In this regard, the JS-SEZ offers an opportunity to create a more integrated economic ecosystem by leveraging the complementary strengths of Johor and Singapore.
"Johor has the opportunity to combine advantages in land, industrial capacity, talent, and cost with Singapore's strengths in capital, technology, business services, and access to international markets.
"However, realising the JS-SEZ potential requires alignment in infrastructure development, energy supply, talent development, customs and immigration processes, and cross-border connectivity," IRDA said.
Olive Tree Property Consultants founder and chief executive officer Samuel Tan said the corridor's next phase would depend on how effectively these complementary advantages could be translated into tangible business benefits.
He said investors were increasingly looking beyond low operating expenses and land availability, with infrastructure readiness, dependable energy supply, access to skilled talent and seamless connectivity becoming critical factors in determining where companies establish or expand their operations.
"The JS-SEZ creates a significant advantage by bringing together complementary strengths that no single jurisdiction could offer in isolation. This includes Johor's abundant land, established industrial capacity, growing talent pool and competitive operating expenses, alongside Singapore's global capital networks, technology, business services and access to international markets," he told Business Times.
However, Tan said the zone's long-term competitiveness would depend on effective coordination between the two jurisdictions, particularly in infrastructure planning, energy security, workforce development and the movement of goods and people across the border.
Streamlining customs and immigration procedures and strengthening physical and digital connectivity would also be essential to improving operational efficiency for businesses operating across both markets.
For Iskandar Malaysia, the challenge is to convert its investment momentum into a more sophisticated economic base that delivers sustained productivity gains, higher-value jobs and greater participation by domestic companies.
The success of the JS-SEZ will therefore be measured not only by its ability to attract more capital but also by how effectively it integrates businesses, develops local talent and strengthens Johor's position in regional and global supply chains.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Minimum 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement retained - Economy Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The minimum 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement remains in place in line with the Property Acquisition Guidelines (GPPH), which took effect on July 13, 2022, and is subject to approval by the Economy Ministry.
The ministry said the government is committed to ensuring that the country's strategic assets, particularly those owned by government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs), contribute more effectively to the Bumiputera economic empowerment agenda.
"The proposed increase in the equity requirement is one of the policy instruments to expand Bumiputera participation and ownership in strategic, high-impact properties, thereby supporting the country's socioeconomic development agenda," the ministry said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
The ministry was responding to questions from Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) on the rationale for increasing the Bumiputera equity quota from 30 to 50 per cent for private companies involved in the disposal of properties worth more than RM20 million by GLCs and GLICs, on the value of transactions affected since the new rule was introduced, and whether the quota could be reverted to 30 per cent.
The ministry said that after taking into account stakeholders' views and reviewing the proposed implementation of the requirement, the government has decided to enforce it through administrative measures to ensure that all GLCs and GLICs implement the Bumiputera economic empowerment agenda.
"The government will continue to monitor the implementation of policies on property acquisition and disposal, and periodically assess the effectiveness of the instruments used to ensure that the Bumiputera economic empowerment agenda is achieved effectively, while taking into account economic developments and current needs," it added.

Title: Retiree sells house, loses RM132,590 in forex scam
Article:
TELUK INTAN: A 73-year-old retiree lost RM132,590 in a bogus foreign exchange (forex) investment scheme, with part of the money coming from the sale of his house.
The victim was lured into the scheme by an acquaintance who promised lucrative returns, prompting him to invest money in stages over about two months.
Hilir Perak district police chief assistant commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the victim lodged a police report on Monday after realising that he had likely fallen victim to the scam.
"Preliminary investigations found that the victim began investing in the scheme on July 4 after being introduced to it by the acquaintance.
"Convinced by promises of high returns, the retiree continued investing until the total amount reached RM132,590," he said in a statement today.
However, Chua said the victim became suspicious when he could no longer access the investment system on Sept 14.
"He also failed to receive any profits or a refund of his capital, as promised. Part of the money invested came from the proceeds of the sale of his house," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Chua said police were conducting further investigations to identify those involved in the alleged scam.
He also advised the public to exercise caution when dealing with investment schemes promising high returns within a short period.
He advised potential investors to verify the legitimacy of investment offers with Bank Negara Malaysia and the Securities Commission Malaysia before parting with their money.
"The public is also reminded not to use retirement savings, proceeds from asset sales or money meant for daily expenses for investments whose legitimacy has not been verified.
"Those who suspect they have been scammed should immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre at 997 and lodge a police report to enable further action," he said.

Title: Early savings pave the way for a child's future
Article:
A CHILD'S future is full of possibilities. Many children start developing their ambitions and dreams young.
For parents, preparing for their children's future is not something that can be achieved overnight. It requires early planning and consistent effort, including setting aside savings for their education.
Through Bulan Menabung Simpan SSPN (BMS) 2026, the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is highlighting the importance of saving as a key step parents can take to prepare for their children's education future.
BMS 2026 runs from Sept 25 to Nov 1, with the theme "Under the Sea". The campaign likens the savings journey to exploring the depths of the ocean, where countless wonders and possibilities await discovery.
The deeper one dives, the more there is to discover. Similarly, a child's journey through life presents numerous opportunities and possibilities.
Some children dream of becoming doctors, teachers, engineers, entrepreneurs or athletes, while others aspire to pursue creative careers.
Each dream comes with its own journey and education is one of the key foundations that can help prepare children for the future.
Every contribution to a child's savings is a small but meaningful step towards helping them achieve their ambitions.
Parents do not need to wait until they have accumulated a substantial amount before they start saving. What matters most is taking the first step early and developing a consistent saving habit.
When it comes to shaping children's future, parents can become real-life superheroes, always standing behind them, offering support and providing for their needs.
Saving for education is not merely about setting aside money. It also reflects parents' love, commitment and determination to secure a better future for their children.
Although children may not yet understand the importance of savings, the efforts parents make from an early age can help prepare them for when they are ready to pursue further education.
Through the tagline "Jom Jadi Superhero Anak Anda!", BMS 2026 encourages parents to play their role in everyday life.
A superhero does not need to wear a costume or have extraordinary powers. To a child, a superhero can be a mother or father who is willing to plan ahead, make sacrifices and prepare for the future to give them the opportunity to pursue their dreams.
Preparing for a child's future can begin with one simple step today: saving.
Every contribution serves a purpose, every step carries meaning and every childhood dream deserves to be supported by careful preparation.
Through BMS 2026, parents are reminded that their children's future is not something they must wait to discover. Instead, they can begin exploring the possibilities today, one savings contribution at a time.
Parents are encouraged to take part in the BMS 2026 Closing Programme, which will be held from Oct 29 to Nov 1 at the Centre Court, Alamanda Shopping Mall, Putrajaya.

Title: 22 areas record unhealthy air quality, Bukit Rambai highest at 174 API
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the affected areas were in Johor, Negri Sembilan, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka, Putrajaya, Selangor and Terengganu.
In Johor, the areas with unhealthy air quality readings were Batu Pahat (157), Larkin (155), Tangkak (153), Pasir Gudang (152), Kluang (151), Segamat (123) and Kota Tinggi (111).
In Negri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (161), Seremban (158) and Port Dickson (155).
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras each recorded an API reading of 159, while Putrajaya recorded 158.
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai recorded an API reading of 174, followed by Bandaraya Melaka (162) and Alor Gajah (158).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded 160, followed by Klang and Banting (159), Shah Alam (158) and Petaling Jaya (157). In Terengganu, Paka recorded 153.
Meanwhile, APIMS data showed that 39 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while seven areas recorded good air quality.
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Takiyuddin challenges Bersatu Youth to prove allegations over PN deregistration
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has challenged Bersatu Youth to substantiate its allegations against him and PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar over the coalition's deregistration.
He said Bersatu Youth had the right to express its views but should provide evidence to support its claims instead of making allegations against the two leaders.
"We challenge him (Bersatu Youth information chief Harris Idaham Rashid) to prove his allegations.
"He has the right to say whatever he wants, but he should not make allegations against me and Samsuri.
"When both of us held positions in PN, there were no problems. PN even won several seats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections," he said.
Takiyuddin was speaking at the Ceramah Jelajah Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah (Himpak), held in conjunction with the 36th anniversary celebrations of Kelantan Membangun Bersama Islam in Pasir Tumboh last night.
Yesterday, Bersatu Youth blamed Takiyuddin and Samsuri for the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS).
Harris has claimed that the crisis stemmed from failures to manage meeting procedures and comply with PN's constitution.
Meanwhile, Takiyuddin said PN was confident of winning the seats it contests in the upcoming Melaka election.
He said although seat allocation among the parties had yet to be finalised, PN would ensure that its candidates would not clash with those fielded by Barisan Nasional.
RoS yesterday confirmed it had
cancelled PN's registration,
saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
The decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after the department reviewed documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil rises on Middle East supply worries
Article:
BEIJING: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday on Middle East supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$109.64 per barrel as of 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$98.58 per barrel.
A supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz while "violating" Iranian regulations, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Tuesday, according to Iranian media. There were at least 18 vessel attacks reported over two weeks, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday.
"Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz," LSEG analysts said in a note. "Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on."
The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia's Riyadh and Abha airports.
The death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified.
Prices had fallen in the previous trading session after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts in a meeting with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran.
On Tuesday, Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at US$108.79, after touching a five-month high of US$111.99. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled down US$1.87, or 1.8 per cent, at US$101.79.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.
In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners around the world to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices.
US crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week along with product inventories, an extended Reuters poll showed on Tuesday. Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that crude inventories fell by about 800,000 barrels in the week ended Oct 16.

Title: 6,346 MyKiosk units operational nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 6,346 MyKiosk units nationwide, or 88 per cent of the 7,243 units provided under the programme, were occupied and operational as of August.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the remaining 897 units, or 12 per cent, were vacant, based on data and operational reports submitted by state governments and local authorities.
"The MyKiosk programme, implemented through the Local Government Department, aims to improve the socioeconomic status of local traders by providing standardised, safe and conducive business premises at affordable rental rates," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website yesterday.
A total of RM150 million was allocated under the 2023 and 2024 Budgets for MyKiosk 1.0 and 2.0, covering 7,243 units nationwide.
Nga said the ministry was working closely with local authorities to increase occupancy rates and ensure the kiosks were fully utilised, with four strategic measures being implemented to address vacancies.
These included establishing an internal task force to conduct regular, coordinated inspections to assess the suitability of kiosk locations and expedite the process of filling vacant units.
He said the ministry was also holding targeted discussions with local authorities to resolve local issues and allowing them to apply for additional allocations for kiosk maintenance and repairs.
"In addition, a strict traffic-light system has been introduced, with MyKiosk occupancy performance used as a benchmark for approving future projects.
"Local authorities recording poor occupancy performance, classified under the Red Zone, will not be considered for approval of new projects."
Nga said ensuring every MyKiosk unit was fully utilised remained a priority, adding that the ministry would continue to implement interventions, monitoring and follow-up measures with local authorities to improve occupancy rates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt open to RCI into KWAP, EPF if evidence warrants probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to considering a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the Retirement Fund Incorporated (KWAP) and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) if credible information or evidence warrants a comprehensive and independent investigation.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said issues involving the management of public funds, including governance and investment decisions, would continue to be examined based on facts and evidence through appropriate oversight mechanisms.
"Should further scrutiny establish a clear need and public interest in a special investigation, the proposal to establish an RCI may be considered accordingly," she said in a written parliamentary reply.
Azalina was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim (Pas-Arau), who asked whether the government was prepared to consider an RCI into KWAP and EPF over governance, investment management or questionable financial decisions.
Shahidan also sought clarification on the criteria used by the government to determine whether an RCI was necessary for institutions managing public funds.
Azalina said the establishment of an RCI was subject to the Commissions of Inquiry Act 1950 and procedures prescribed by the government.
"Under the standard operating procedures, a proposal to establish an RCI must be submitted through a Cabinet Memorandum by the lead ministry for consideration and approval by the Cabinet.
"Once approved, the prime minister will submit the proposal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for royal consent.
"Upon obtaining consent, the RCI's terms of reference, membership and duration of the inquiry will be determined and finalised through publication in the Federal Government Gazette before it begins its work," she said.
She said the government would consider the public interest, seriousness of the issues, available facts and evidence, and the need for an independent and comprehensive investigation when deciding whether to establish an RCI, whether into institutions managing public funds or any other institution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global seabed mapping
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Malaysia is strengthening its role in global seabed mapping by hosting an international meeting and data sprint. The event brings together experts from 33 countries to advance ocean mapping and data sharing.
Royal Malaysian Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain officiated at the opening of the Seabed 2030 Indo-Pacific Ocean Mapping Meeting and Data Sprint 2026 here.
The event saw the signing of a memorandum of understanding on the Melaka and Singapore Straits Electronic Navigational Charts and a Seabed 2030 data-sharing agreement.
The signatories included National Hydrographic Centre  director-general Rear Admiral Dr Najhan Md Said, Indonesian Navy Hydro-Oceanographic Centre (Pushidrosal) Commodore Edward Halomoan Sibuea and Japan Hydrographic Association representative Dr Masayuki Fujita. A representative of Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority and Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project director Jamie McMichael-Phillips also signed the agreements.
Organised by the NHC, the event has attracted 250 participants from 33 countries, including hydrographers, government representatives, research institutions and maritime industry players.
The plenary session runs until today, followed by a data sprint today and tomorrow. The sprint provides hands-on experience in preparing, demonstrating and integrating bathymetric data.
Zulhelmy said the ocean was central to Malaysia's identity, economy and security.
"For Malaysia, the ocean is fundamental to who we are. Our geography, economy, security and future are inseparable from the maritime domain.
"Effective maritime policy begins with knowledge. We cannot manage what we do not understand. We cannot protect what we cannot see."
The Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project aims to accelerate the mapping of the world's seabed by 2030. Up to April, only 28.7 per cent of the ocean floor had been mapped to modern standards, leaving more than 70 per cent inadequately mapped.
"This is a significant knowledge gap with implications for science, development and security," said Zulhelmy.
He thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the allocation in the 2027 Budget to acquire two new survey motor launches, saying the vessels would expedite hydrographic survey operations and help address priority data gaps.
Zulhelmy also thanked the National Security Council  for facilitating approval for Malaysia's first national research vessel, describing it as a strategic investment in the country's maritime future.
On data sharing, he said arrangements must respect national requirements, security considerations, data ownership and agreed conditions of use.
"This gathering can boost  Malaysia's role as a regional hub for seabed mapping and marine geospatial cooperation," he said.
In a separate address, Najhan said the meeting built on a Seabed 2030 gathering held in Nadi, Fiji, in 2024.
"I sincerely hope that every delegate will return home with valuable insights, new skills and practical experiences."

Title: Haj waiting period could fall from 150 years to below 70
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The haj waiting period could be more than halved, from about 150 years to less than 70, under the Haj Preparation Plan – Seruan Istito'ah.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the projected reduction was based on current estimates by Lembaga Tabung Haji, but could change depending on several factors.
"This depends on several factors, including the number of depositors who meet the prescribed minimum savings requirement, Malaysia's official haj quota in the future and developments in the Holy Land.
"Depositors who had already registered for haj would be given a transition period of more than two years, until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings requirement of RM15,000.
"From Jan 1, 2029, the haj waiting list will be systematically and automatically reorganised according to registration dates among depositors who have achieved the minimum savings threshold," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Zulkifli was responding to Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (Pas-Kuala Krai), who asked about the actual waiting period for depositors who had reached the RM15,000 minimum savings threshold, as well as the status of those who had registered long ago but had yet to accumulate the required amount.
Zulkifli said depositors who had registered but had yet to meet the RM15,000 requirement would be included in the active haj waiting list once they fulfilled the savings requirement.

Title: Ringgit opens higher on strong domestic economic data
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by strong domestic economic data that strengthened expectations of a possible normalisation of the overnight policy rate (OPR).
At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0795/0850 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0805/0845.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said robust economic indicators, particularly export growth and gross domestic product (GDP) expansion, provide support for the local currency.
"Strong data points for the Malaysian economy have raised the odds of a possible OPR normalisation. The latest trade data showed exports jumped 54.5 per cent in September, while GDP grew 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, exceeding consensus forecasts," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam added that easing expectations of a US interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's October meeting contributed to a 0.27 per cent fall in the US Dollar Index to 101.707 points, further supporting the ringgit.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies.
It gained versus the Japanese yen to 2.5772/5809 from 2.5803/5830 at Tuesday's close, but fell against the British pound to 5.4551/4625 from 5.4475/4528 and edged down against the euro to 4.5796/5858 from 4.5771/5816.
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It traded marginally higher versus the Indonesian rupiah at 226.7/227.1 from 226.8/227.1, and gained slightly against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.48 from 6.47/6.48.
The local currency was lower against the Thai baht to 12.1341/1577 from 12.1241/1411 at yesterday's close and depreciated versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1918/1964 from 3.1914/1950.

Title: New MyKad's security, efforts to tackle cross-border haze among topics in Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The justification for introducing a new-generation MyKad, its security levels, and cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia in tackling cross-border haze are among topics expected to take center stage during the Dewan Rakyat sitting today.
According to the Order Paper, during the question-and-answer session, Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) will ask the home minister to explain the extent to which enhanced security features, chip technology, and identity verification systems on the new MyKad can combat forgery, cloning, and the misuse of citizens' identities, while ensuring their personal data remains protected.
Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar) wants the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability to explain the diplomatic actions and cooperation implemented by the Malaysian government with the Indonesian government to mitigate the risk of cross-border haze.
Also expected to draw attention is a question from Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong) to the investment, trade and industry regarding the latest status minister of the initiative to produce 60,000 skilled workers in the semiconductor field under the National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS), including the number of individuals trained and the budget spent so far.
Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (Bersatu-Masjid Tanah) will ask the entrepreneur development and cooperatives minister to state the percentage of micro-entrepreneurs who received financing and assistance from the ministry's agencies from 2023 to 2026, those who successfully upgraded their business category to small or medium enterprises (SMEs), and the business failure rate after three years.
Additionally, Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) will pose a question to the transport minister regarding the full implementation schedule of the open payment system for all public transportation services in the Klang Valley.
Following the question-and-answer session, the sitting is scheduled to proceed with the tabling of the Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons (Amendment) Bill 2026 for its first reading by the home minister.
The sitting will then resume the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage following the
tabling of 2027 Budget
by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, on Oct 9.
Based on the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on 2027 Budget runs from Oct 12 to 22, prior to the winding-up sessions by relevant ministers for four days beginning Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until Dec 8.

Title: US coaxing refiners to produce more diesel as prices surge, energy officials say
Article:
TITUSVILLE/HOUSTON: Two top US Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners at home and abroad to boost fuel output as a diesel shortage has raised prices, driving dissatisfaction among voters with the White House ahead of the November midterm elections.
Diesel prices have jumped to record highs because of disruptions from the Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries . Retail diesel prices averaged about US$6.32 a gallon on Tuesday, according to motorist group AAA.
The Trump administration has taken several steps to try to lower fuel prices that have surged since the start of the Iran war on Feb 28, including relaxing restrictions on Russian diesel exports, invoking the Defense Production Act to boost output and allowing commercial vehicles to run on red-dyed diesel normally limited to off-road equipment.
Diesel is critical to the global economy, powering much of the transport, agriculture and heavy industry that underpin global trade and economic activity. The high cost of fuel has soured voters on US President Donald Trump's stewardship of the economy, with 36 per cent approving of Trump on that issue, according to the most recent Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll.
"We are talking about reopening every refinery we can," Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in Houston. "There are dialogues there, and that's a tough challenge. I'm not saying all these are going to happen."
DIFFICULT TO RAISE US OUTPUT
US refineries are running near full capacity, and with several facilities shutting in recent years, there is little leeway to quickly boost domestic output, analysts say.
Refinery expansions are capital intensive and take months, if not years, to complete depending on the complexity of the additions.
Wright said the US is also working with India to increase refining output there to bring products to global markets.
American Petroleum Institute chief executive officer Mike Sommers told Reuters on the sidelines of an energy forum in Titusville, Pennsylvania that US refiners are running at 95 per cent to 100 per cent of capacity. He said they are putting off planned maintenance because of high prices.
"The American refiners are doing everything they can," Sommers said. He said that using the Defense Production Act to restart idled plants, as the administration has floated, would require a lot of capital.
Last week, Vice President JD Vance said the administration would use the Defense Production Act to expand capacity of a Texas refinery owned by Delek US Holdings.
Trump signed legislation last year that included US$1 billion in Defense Production Act funding for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security.
Wright said there was "more to do" on refining and the Defense Production Act but did not provide additional details.
Sommers singled out China's spare refining capacity, saying their government is currently barring diesel exports. Beijing "is really going to be the key if we're going to get long-term prices down," he said.
A spokesperson for theChinese embassy in Washington said the key to resolving the issue is to achieve a ceasefire in Iran. "China stands ready to maintain communication with all sides to jointly safeguard global energy security and keep industrial and supply chains stable," the spokesperson added.
PUSH FOR EUROPEAN DIESEL
Trump temporarily waived sanctions this month on Russian diesel in an attempt to lower prices. Russian diesel will likely move to New England, if it moves to the US at all, Wright said. Already, cargoes from Russia are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions, with two tankers signaling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, Reuters reported on Tuesday.
The Trump administration has also been pushing Europe to release more fuel to balance global markets.
"We are working with our friends ... to find new and innovative ways to get more throughput" through refineries, said Energy Department Under Secretary Kyle Haustveit at the Drake Forum in Titusville.
While the Trump administration has pushed Europe to release 50 million barrels of diesel, an agreement by industrialised nations fell short of that target. The Paris-based International Energy Agency (IEA) said last week it would speed the release of crude ​and oil product volumes pledged in March, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible.
Fatih Birol, chief of the IEA, which coordinates industrialised nations' releases ​of oil from emergency stocks, said on Tuesday the group ‌is ready to coordinate more oil releases by member countries if needed.

Title: MCBA chief arrives at court over alleged assault on two policemen [WATCH]
Article:
SEPANG: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain arrived at the court complex to face two charges over an alleged assault involving two Special Branch policemen.
Security was tight at the court complex, with a heavy presence of police personnel and Rela members.
Only court staff and police personnel were allowed to park within the compound.
Shuhaily, dressed in a suit, appeared in high spirits as he walked into the canteen for breakfast, even inviting journalists and photographers to join him.
Also present in a show of solidarity was Port Klang MCBA commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
Shuhaily, 54, is expected to face two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporals Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman in connection with a Sept 28 incident at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1.
The charges, under Section 323 of the Penal Code, carry a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Shuhaily will be represented by lawyer Kitson Foong.
On Oct 17, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) had requested further clarification and additional investigative work before deciding on the next course of action.
He said police had been directed to complete the investigation in accordance with the AGC's requirements.
The investigation papers were initially submitted to the AGC after police recorded statements from 25 witnesses.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said he received the papers on Oct 6 before returning them to police on Oct 8.
On Oct 12, Faiz lodged a second police report alleging that his mobile phone had been seized while he was taking photographs of the incident.
His lawyers, Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin, said the report contained new evidence.
The two policemen, who were serving as travel control officers at the airport, have denied allegations that they were acting as touts or involved in "counter setting".
The incident drew public attention after a video circulated online showing a man resembling Shuhaily berating two men at the airport. One of the men appeared to be grabbed forcefully by the ears.
On Oct 1, Shuhaily said he was prepared to accept whatever decision the government made over the incident and was ready to take responsibility for his actions.

Title: Malaysians to gain from wider access to affordable essentials
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians will benefit from wider access to affordable essentials, improved distribution in rural areas and stronger consumer protection under the 2027 Budget, as the government steps up efforts to address the rising cost of living.
The RM80 billion allocation for aid, subsidies and incentives aims to ease financial pressures on households while supporting businesses, rural entrepreneurs and the creative industry.
The measures, backed by additional funding for affordable sales programmes and enforcement, intends to make essential goods more accessible, improve market fairness and create new economic opportunities.
The allocation for the Program Jualan Rahmah Madani (PJRM) and Program Jualan Agro Madani will increase from RM630 million to RM750 million, supporting 35,000 sales events nationwide.
The fund will cover 30,000 Rahmah Sales programmes and 5,000 Agro Sales programmes.
The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry will prioritise rural communities, low-cost housing areas and People's Housing Programme developments.
Greater participation by grocery shops and vending machine operators, alongside wholesale sales events, will make discounted goods more accessible.
For households, this means more opportunities to purchase necessities at lower prices.
Small traders are expected to benefit from the PJRM Borong, which aims to improve access to supplies and reduce inventory costs. Lower operating costs can help traders sustain their businesses and offer goods at more competitive prices.
BETTER ACCESS IN RURAL AREAS
An allocation of RM250 million to expand the distribution of essential goods to rural and remote areas will help address supply challenges faced by underserved communities.
The initiative will cover six new locations: Kampung Buayan, Kampung Terian, Kaiduan, Kundasang and Kampung Nibang in Sabah, as well as Kampung Dato Godam in Sarawak.
More reliable distribution networks can reduce the need for rural folk to travel long distances to obtain necessities, easing their transport costs and logistical burdens.
The initiative aims to narrow the gap between urban and remote communities in terms of access to essential goods.
NEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR BUSINESSES
Rural entrepreneurs stand to benefit from the RM10 million allocation for Jom Beli Produk Malaysia (Jom Malaysia), formerly known as Kempen Beli Barangan Malaysia, to encourage people to support Malaysian products.
The initiative will help businesses promote their products and high-value services through digital platforms and explore domestic and international markets.
For small businesses with limited market access, greater online exposure can help them reach more customers, increase sales and develop new revenue streams.
Consumers can contribute to the growth of local businesses by choosing Malaysian products, while entrepreneurs gain opportunities to expand their customer base.
[[nid:1560193]]
STRONGER CONSUMER PROTECTION AND FAIRER MARKETS
The 2027 Budget provides RM1.1 billion to strengthen agencies' enforcement capabilities, including the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Malaysia Competition Commission.
The allocation is intended to improve compliance with trade and competition laws, protect consumers and address offences within the jurisdictions of these authorities.
For consumers, more effective enforcement can help safeguard their interests and promote fairer market practices.
The government also plans to table an E-commerce Bill at the next Parliament sitting to strengthen oversight of online platforms and sellers, including foreign operators.
As online shopping becomes more common, the proposed legislation aims to improve accountability and consumer safety while helping micro, small and medium enterprises compete in a fairer digital marketplace.
FOOD DONATIONS AND WASTE REDUCTION
Tax deductions for food and equipment donations to the Ihsan Food Bank Initiative (i-FB), applicable from Jan 1, 2027 to Dec 31, 2030, are intended to encourage businesses to support food redistribution.
The initiative adopts a 3S approach - "Santuni Komuniti, Sayangi Alam, Selamatkan Makanan" (Care for Communities, Love the Environment, Save Food).
By encouraging businesses to donate usable food and equipment, the measure can help direct resources to communities in need while reducing food waste and promoting more responsible resource use.
SUPPORTING CREATIVE TALENT
The government aims to develop 20 new animation intellectual properties and commercialise Malaysian characters internationally.
The initiative can create opportunities for Malaysian creators and businesses to develop marketable content, secure licensing deals and reach audiences abroad.
Stronger intellectual property protection and registration will help creators safeguard their work and increase its commercial value, benefiting businesses in production and related services.
TURNING ALLOCATIONS INTO TANGIBLE BENEFITS
The 2027 Budget's measures cover several aspects of Malaysians' daily lives, from household spending and access to basic necessities to business opportunities and online consumer protection.
Households can benefit from more affordable goods, while rural communities stand to gain from improved distribution.
Small businesses and entrepreneurs can access new markets, while consumers can benefit from stronger enforcement and greater accountability in online transactions.
But the extent of these benefits will depend on effective implementation, with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry playing a key role in ensuring initiatives reach intended recipients.
Through its efforts to improve access to affordable essentials, strengthen consumer protection, enforce trade regulations and support businesses, the ministry will be instrumental in translating 2027 Budget allocations into tangible benefits for households and businesses.
Ultimately, the success of these measures will depend on how effectively the ministry and other agencies implement initiatives to ease the cost of living, promote fairer market practices and strengthen the competitiveness of the domestic economy.

Title: Malaysia posts RM1.57tril exports in nine months, but growth may cool
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's exports hit a record RM1.57 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, but an economist cautions that the headline growth figures alone do not reveal the underlying strength of the country's trade performance.
Exports rose 34 per cent year-on-year, supported by strong electrical and electronics (E&E) shipments and expanding demand in non-traditional markets.
However, Putra Business School professor Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said more detailed data were needed to determine how much of the increase came from higher shipment volumes, prices or a shift towards higher-value products.
"We still need to look at the detailed volume and unit-value data to distinguish these effects and assess the underlying strength of export performance," he told Business Times.
Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade) today said total trade grew 30.1 per cent to RM2.91 trillion during the period, while imports increased 25.7 per cent to RM1.34 trillion.
This resulted in a trade surplus of RM232.38 billion.
E&E products remained the main export driver, contributing an increase of RM253.88 billion amid global demand linked to artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology adoption.
Other contributors included petroleum products, optical and scientific equipment, machinery, equipment and parts, as well as liquefied natural gas.
Downstream palm oil-based manufactured products, particularly oleochemicals, also recorded double-digit export growth.
Meanwhile, automotive parts and accessories, pharmaceutical products, metal furniture and aerospace products posted positive growth.
These industries also feature significant participation from Malaysian small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Ahmed Razman expects export growth to moderate in 2027 as global demand normalises and the high base of comparison makes further gains harder to achieve.
He said Malaysia could maintain a positive export trajectory if semiconductor demand, AI-related investment and E&E production remained strong.
However, weaker global economic growth, geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions could weigh on the outlook.
Economist Dr Geoffrey Williams expects the strong performance to continue into 2027, citing sustained external demand, higher export prices and increased volumes.
"The strong export demand is further evidence that the standard narrative of global headwinds, Middle East conflict and Trump tariffs is false," Williams said.
AI Demand Drives E&E Exports
The E&E sector remained a major contributor to export growth with exports increasing by RM253.88 billion amid strong global demand linked to AI.
Ahmed Razman said Malaysia's reliance on the semiconductor and AI investment cycle could expose exports to a slowdown in technology spending.
"Sustained investment in AI infrastructure, data centres and advanced computing supports demand for Malaysian electronics," he said.
However, weaker semiconductor demand or a slowdown in technology investment could significantly affect exports, he added.
Ahmed Razman said Malaysia should move towards higher-value semiconductor activities while diversifying its manufacturing base.
Williams identified technology, AI and semiconductors as key drivers alongside traditional sectors such as oil and gas and palm oil.
Beyond E&E, Matrade said petroleum products, optical and scientific equipment, machinery, equipment and parts as well as liquefied natural gas, were contributors to export growth.
Exports of downstream palm oil-based manufactured products, particularly oleochemicals, also recorded double-digit growth.
Other products recording positive growth included automotive parts and accessories, pharmaceutical products, metal furniture and aerospace products, which feature substantial participation from Malaysian SMEs.
Higher Imports Reflect Stronger Activity
The 25.7 per cent increase in imports could indicate stronger manufacturing activity and investment although their composition needs further examination.
Ahmed Razman said the increase suggested stronger demand for intermediate inputs, machinery and capital equipment.
"It also reflects Malaysia's deep integration into global supply chains, where imported components are processed or assembled before being exported," he added.
However, he said imports should be assessed by category to distinguish productive investment from consumption and inventory accumulation.
Williams said imports reflected stronger domestic activity including goods brought into Malaysia for re-export and purchases by consumers.
Market Diversification Continues
Exports to non-traditional markets across Africa, Central Asia, South Asia and Latin America rose 21.5 per cent to RM136.36 billion in the first nine months of 2026.
Exports to Namibia surged 426.1 per cent, while shipments to South Africa increased 101 per cent, Libya 79.3 per cent, Angola 55.6 per cent and Brazil 41 per cent.
Ahmed Razman said the growth was encouraging but insufficient to substantially reduce Malaysia's reliance on established trading partners.
He said Malaysia should expand market access through trade agreements, stronger business networks and targeted export promotion.
"Crucially, diversification must involve a broader range of products and industries, not simply more destinations for the same exports," he said.
Williams said expanding into non-traditional markets would gradually reduce Malaysia's reliance on established trading partners.
Malaysia's free trade agreement (FTA) partners accounted for RM986.38 billion or 62.8 per cent of total exports with shipments to these markets growing 25.8 per cent.
Exports to 21 of Malaysia's 24 FTA partners increased, led by Mexico at 52.1 per cent, Vietnam at 44.9 per cent, the United Kingdom at 41.1 per cent and Thailand at 32.3 per cent.

Title: Malaysia mulls CPO tax waiver as palm oil stocks hit record 3.5mil tonnes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is considering waiving the crude palm oil (CPO) export tax to help clear record-high stockpiles and narrow the pricing gap with Indonesia.
The move aims to make Malaysian exports more competitive and help producers regain lost market share.
The proposal comes as Malaysia's palm oil inventories climbed to 3.5 million tonnes last month, putting growing pressure on exporters because Indonesian palm oil continues to enjoy a significant price advantage.
According to a wire report, the government is considering the waiver. The Plantation and Commodities Ministry is expected to discuss the proposal with industry players.
Beyond offering short-term relief to plantation companies, the proposed waiver raises a bigger question: Can lower export costs boost shipments, improve producer prices and increase foreign exchange earnings without significantly denting government revenue?
ESG Malaysia executive director Dr Harald Sippel said a temporary waiver of crude palm oil (CPO) export tax could help Malaysia reduce swelling inventories and boost exports.
However, it is unlikely to close the price gap with Indonesia or deliver lasting competitiveness.
Sippel said Malaysia's 3.5 million tonnes of palm oil stocks will require broader measures to clear, as Indonesian palm oil remained significantly cheaper despite the country imposing higher export duties and levies.
Malaysia's 10 per cent export tax amounts to about RM450 a tonne at current prices, while Indonesian palm oil trades RM700 to RM900 a tonne cheaper.
"Even if every ringgit of the waiver were passed on to buyers, it would close only half to two-thirds of that gap," he told Business Times.
Sippel said Indonesia could also lower its levy in response to falling exports, potentially offsetting Malaysia's move.
The waiver could nevertheless lift shipments in the short term, particularly to price-sensitive markets such as India.
He said Malaysia could clear stocks more quickly by combining the waiver with measures to boost domestic demand, particularly through higher biodiesel blending.
On the fiscal impact, Sippel estimated that every million tonnes of CPO exported tax-free would cost the Treasury about RM450 million at current prices.
Some of the revenue loss could be recovered through higher corporate tax and windfall levy receipts, but not all.
He said any waiver should have a firm end date and clear exit conditions to prevent temporary relief from becoming a permanent subsidy.
Plantation companies will benefit from higher domestic CPO prices, while smallholders could gain from improved fresh fruit bunch prices if mills passed on the increases.
However, downstream processors could lose out as removing the crude oil tax would erode the cost advantage enjoyed by Malaysia's refining industry.
Refiners will face higher feedstock costs while competing with Malaysian crude palm oil in export markets, Sippel said.
He said a time-limited waiver could support prices by helping clear stocks, but lasting competitiveness would depend on better yields, replanting, labour productivity and stronger supply-chain traceability.
The latter is becoming increasingly important as the European Union's Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) requires palm oil sold in the bloc to be traceable to plots of land and supported by evidence that they were not deforested after 2020.
Sippel said Malaysia could not assume it would automatically gain an advantage over Indonesia, as the EU classified both countries as standard risk in its risk benchmarking.
Malaysia must demonstrate traceability across shipments, including those sourced from smallholders, who face the same geolocation requirements as large plantation groups but have fewer resources to meet them, he said.
He suggested that the government and industry consider using part of the revenue forgone through the waiver to map smallholder farms and strengthen traceability systems.
Although the EU buys less Malaysian palm oil than India or China, stronger traceability could help exporters meet the requirements of global consumer goods companies that increasingly apply EU-level standards across their supply chains.
Sippel said the waiver could provide temporary breathing space, but Malaysia's long-term competitiveness would depend on improving productivity and proving the origin of its palm oil rather than competing on price alone.
Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) analyst Chong Hoe Leong said the potential waiver will likely be welcomed by the industry and could help Malaysia regain market share from Indonesia.
"We believe the (prospect) will be well received and likely will take effect soon. Such a waiver of the CPO export tax will help Malaysia regain market share from Indonesia," he said in a note.
At present, Malaysia imposes a 10 per cent CPO export tax, while Indonesia's combined export duty and levy stands at US$273 per tonne (RM1,113 per tonne).
The difference in export costs has contributed to Indonesian CPO trading at a discount of RM700 to RM900 per tonne against Malaysian prices, putting local exporters at a competitive disadvantage.
"This wide discount has put Malaysia's CPO exporters at a disadvantage, resulting in a significant loss of market share to our counterparts and a record inventory level of 3.5 million tonnes last month.
"This is evident as Indonesian palm oil exports have grown, in contrast to Malaysia's lacklustre performance," Chong said.
For economists, the central question is whether removing the export tax will narrow the price gap sufficiently to stimulate demand and accelerate inventory clearance, or whether other factors, including global demand, competing vegetable oil prices and Indonesia's export policies, will continue to constrain Malaysia's competitiveness.
The impact on government revenue would also need to be weighed against the potential economic benefits of higher export volumes, improved cash flow for producers and stronger activity across the palm oil supply chain.
Malaysia previously waived its CPO export tax for six months in 2020.
Chong suggested that any new waiver should remain in place until domestic inventories fall below two million tonnes.
The proposal could also have uneven implications for industry players.
Upstream plantation companies could benefit from stronger export demand and improved CPO prices, while downstream processors may face margin pressure if greater export availability pushes up the cost of their raw materials.
The policy's effectiveness would therefore depend not only on the tax reduction itself, but also on how much of the savings exporters pass on to buyers and whether stronger demand translates into better prices received by Malaysian producers.
Meanwhile, plantation companies are heading into their third-quarter 2026 results season with support from stronger production and higher average CPO prices.
Chong said all plantation companies under PublicInvest's coverage recorded production growth, led by Ta Ann Holdings Bhd, whose fresh fruit bunch (FFB) output rose 30 per cent year-on-year.
Sarawak Plantation Bhd followed with 23.2 per cent growth, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd recorded a 16.4 per cent increase.
Average CPO prices rose to RM4,552 per tonne in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RM4,275 per tonne in the corresponding period last year.
The combination of higher output, lower production costs and firmer selling prices is expected to support earnings in the second half of the year.
Chong maintains an "Overweight" rating on the plantation sector, naming Sarawak Plantation and Ta Ann as his preferred picks because of their attractive dividend yields and above-industry-average FFB production growth.
