Title: Guan Eng warns of SME liquidity crisis over RM30b delayed tax refunds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Former finance minister Lim Guan Eng has urged the federal government to expedite the repayment of RM29.919 billion in tax refund arrears, warning that holding back businesses’ own money severely strains corporate liquidity, particularly among struggling small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Lim, who is the member of parliament for Bagan, pointed to the 2025 Federal Government Financial Statements, which show that outstanding tax refund liabilities decreased by RM3.425 billion, dropping from RM33.342 billion in 2024 to RM29.919 billion in 2025.
While acknowledging the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) for whittling down the balance owed to firms that overpaid their taxes, Lim stressed that the outstanding sum remains colossal by any benchmark, especially since it belongs to the private sector.
“In 2026, RM9 billion was paid to 130,000 companies by Sept 30,” he noted, adding that the government must repay companies, especially the 1.2 million SMEs, more quickly.
To curb systemic delays, Lim proposed placing a strict RM10 billion cap on federal tax refund arrears. He argued that allowing the backlog to hover near RM30 billion inflicts undue financial hardship on cash-strapped businesses wrestling with deteriorating operating environments and a volatile global economic climate.
Historical data demonstrates a steady accumulation over recent years, Lim said. Outstanding tax refund commitments stood at RM21.836 billion in 2021, before climbing to RM25.721 billion in 2022 and RM25.511 billion in 2023.
The DAP lawmaker also took direct aim at public officials tasked with safeguarding small businesses, questioning why statutory agency leaders have failed to advocate forcefully for the immediate release of these funds.
“Failing to consistently and persistently press the government to return back to SMEs their own money, may give the unfortunate impression that those responsible and holding statutory positions are ‘sleeping on the job’.”
Lim also pointed out that statutory late-payment penalties have surged sharply as a consequence of refund delays. Under Section 111D of the Income Tax Act, the government is mandated to pay an annual 2 per cent compensation to taxpayers when IRB fails to disburse excess tax refunds within stipulated timeframes.
While IRB disbursed RM23.64 million under this mechanism in 2025, that penalty figure escalated by nearly fivefold in the first nine months of 2026 alone, hitting RM109 million as of Sept 30.

Title: Perak Perhilitan monitoring elephant herd after crop destruction complaints
Article:
IPOH, Oct 21 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has received six official complaints this year from oil palm smallholders in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, over wild elephants destroying crops and plantation infrastructure.
Its director, Dr Pazil Abdul Patah, said the herd is estimated at between three and eight elephants, believed to have come from the nearby Korbu Forest Reserve.
"The herd encroaching on Kampung Perlop 1 originally came from the Piah Forest Reserve in Lenggong, which has an estimated total of about 50 elephants, but has now split into smaller groups.
"Perhilitan also believes these are the same elephants that encroached into fruit orchards around Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, on Oct 15, as both locations fall within the range of the Korbu Forest Reserve," he said in a statement.
Yesterday, 18 oil palm smallholders appealed for urgent intervention from the authorities to tackle incursions by the mammals, which have destroyed crops spanning 80 hectares since early September.
Earlier, 12 farmers in Bukit Bangkong similarly appealed to the authorities for action to protect their 9.7-hectare fruit orchards from persistent elephant threats.
Meanwhile, Pazil said the department is actively monitoring the herd's movements to determine the most effective approach to resolve the conflict.
"For the long term, the department will focus on identifying conflict hotspots, strengthening early reporting systems, and expanding community awareness programmes," he said.
Pazil also advised affected smallholders to report incidents promptly to Perak Perhilitan so that applications under the Property and Crop Damage Assistance (BKHT) scheme can be processed in accordance with established requirements.
He said applicants should provide details including the plantation's location, the type and estimated cost of damage, the date of the incident, and supporting documents such as photographs and proof of land ownership or tenancy. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia calls for WHO-led pooled medicine purchasing amid supply risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed that the World Health Organisation (WHO) Western Pacific Region (WPRO) urgently pilot a pooled procurement project for selected medicines to ensure drug security in the region.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the move was urgent as almost the entire region is facing critical challenges due to disrupted supply chains, market uncertainty, and high reliance on Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) imports, with international geopolitical conflicts worsening the situation.
“Regional diplomacy and solidarity today must be translated beyond mere expressions of good intentions. To protect the survival of health systems in the Western Pacific, we demand a strategic, bold shift in action focused on tangible, measurable results,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Dzulkefly presented the proposal at the Ministerial Roundtable held in conjunction with the 77th WHO WPRO Regional Committee Meeting.
He said the pooled procurement pilot project must involve selected medicines with healthy supplier competition and clear shared needs, and must be implemented transparently.
To support the mechanism, Dzulkefly proposed developing an ASEAN Medicines Security Dashboard as an early warning system linking pricing information with supply distribution, stock availability, and manufacturing capacity.
He also stressed that price monitoring alone could not absolutely guarantee medicine security.
Instead, he said the region needs a strategic manufacturing alliance through joint investment initiatives to cover production gaps.
“To realise this major framework, it requires clear leadership from a lead country under the 2026-2030 Plan, complete with funding accountability and clear key performance indicators,” he said.
Domestically, he said Malaysia has institutionalised pooled procurement across government health facilities, maintained a three-month medicine buffer stock, and spearheaded the ASEAN Drug Security and Self-Reliance (ADSSR) initiative.
He added that Malaysia would continue to leverage global health diplomacy platforms to ensure uninterrupted treatment for the people. — Bernama

Title: Corporate-creative collaborations vital to boost Malaysian IPs, says Teo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Collaborations between corporate entities and local creative talent are vital in driving the growth of Malaysia’s creative sector and showcasing homegrown intellectual properties (IPs) to a broader audience.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said such strategic collaborations between corporate entities and homegrown creative teams allow local artists, animators, performers, and production personnel to showcase their skills on a wider stage.
“Usually, when we speak about local animation and creative content, we think of something we watch on television, in the cinema, or on our phones. Today, we get to walk into the story, meet its characters, and experience the world our own creators have imagined,” she said.
Speaking at The Haunted Highlands 2026 Press Conference and Exclusive Media Preview at Pavilion Hall, Skytropolis Indoor Theme Park here today, Teo praised Resorts World Genting for investing in Malaysian talent.
“For our creative industry to grow, we need businesses willing to believe in Malaysian talent and give Malaysian stories room to develop,” she said.
She explained that transforming animated IPs into physical attractions demonstrates how the creative and tourism sectors can mutually reinforce each other.
“An animated character that audiences first meet on screen can become part of a family’s holiday experience. Visitors may discover the attraction first, then go home and look up the series. That connection helps our creative industry and our tourism industry grow together,” Teo said.
Reiterating the government’s commitment to developing the nation’s Orange Economy, she outlined key allocations under Budget 2027 aimed at driving growth across the creative sector.
“These include allocating over RM130 million to support the creative industry, providing incentives for film and animation productions, exempting local film screenings and theatre performances in the Federal Territories from entertainment duty starting in 2027, and aiming to create 20 new animation intellectual properties (IPs),” she said.
Additionally, she pointed out that funding agencies such as MyCreative Ventures provide financial support through grants, loans, and equity investments across various creative pillars.
She added that eligible local animation film productions can also benefit from the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia’s (FINAS) Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI).
“Successful applicants may receive a 30 per cent cash rebate on qualifying Malaysian production expenditure (QMPE), with an additional rebate of up to five per cent for productions that meet the Malaysian Cultural Test, subject to the applicable terms and conditions,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Port Klang raid exposes alleged subsidised cooking oil diversion scheme
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — The Selangor Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) has successfully uncovered the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods specifically one-kilogramme (kg) packets of cooking oil following a raid on a premises in the Port Klang area, with the seized items valued at RM133,950.
Selangor KPDN director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the suspected modus operandi involved bringing the packets of cooking oil to the premises, where they were mixed with used cooking oil in a dedicated storage tank.
He added that this mixture was allegedly kept for resale to companies that process used cooking oil, or distributed via the black market, in order to generate excessive profits.
“This activity is also believed to involve supplies sourced from parties suspected of holding valid licenses for scheduled controlled goods (CSA). The raid uncovered a large quantity of boxes containing packeted cooking oil, as well as plastic packets that had already been cut open.
“Approximately 15,900 kg of cooking oil, along with various equipment used in this operation including a lorry have been seized for further investigation,” he said yesterday.
Muhamad Hanif stated that the raid was conducted under the integrated ‘Ops Tiris 4.0’ which also involved the Marine Police and resulted in the detention of a foreign national in his 30s, who was employed at the premises, to assist with the investigation.
He added that the case is being investigated under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 [Act 122] and the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA 2001) [Act 613].
“The Selangor KPDN will not compromise with any party found to be involved in such syndicates or illicit activities. We will continue to intensify monitoring and enforcement efforts to ensure that no one exploits or misappropriates subsidised controlled goods intended for the public,” he said. — Bernama

Title: More than 1,500 public toilets upgraded under Housing Ministry initiative
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 —  The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) allocated RM154 million to local authorities (PBT) nationwide from 2023 to 2025 for the maintenance, repair and upgrading of public toilet facilities.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the allocation had enabled 1,529 public toilets under the supervision of local authorities nationwide to be upgraded so far.
He said KPKT would continue these efforts by allocating a special RM30 million annually from 2026 to 2030, bringing the total allocation to RM150 million for the repair and upgrading of public toilets managed by local authorities over the next five years.
Meanwhile, Nga said cooperation between KPKT and the Education Ministry had also resulted in 11,835 school toilets nationwide being upgraded, which he described as the largest achievement of its kind in history.
He said providing public toilets that were clean, attractive and fragrant (BMW) was important to improving the people’s quality of life and reflecting the country’s level of civilisation and image, particularly as Malaysia sought to attract more foreign tourists.
“Public toilets are essentially the calling card at the forefront of a country’s image,” he said when delivering his speech at the Malaysia Best Toilet Awards 2026 (TOTYA’26), organised by KPKT, here tonight.
Also present were Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu, Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh, and Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Marhamah Rosli.
Nga said Malaysia was expected to receive 47 million foreign tourists this year, making the provision of clean and comfortable public toilet facilities an important aspect of supporting the country’s tourism sector.
He said awareness of the importance of public toilet cleanliness had also shown positive growth, with participation in TOTYA’26 increasing to 849 entries this year from 345 in its inaugural year, representing an increase of more than 200 per cent.
Now in its fourth edition, TOTYA’26 features eight categories: schools, places of worship, shopping centres, petrol stations, hotels, restaurants, local authorities, and toilets at rest and recreation (R&R) areas.
Among the winners of TOTYA’26 were Masjid Nurussalam in Gerik, Perak, in the places of worship category; Shah Alam City Council, for the public toilet at Tasik Barat, Section 14, Shah Alam, in the local authorities category; Iconic Marjorie Penang, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel in Bayan Lepas, in the hotel category; and Mamakim Wellness Kitchen Sdn Bhd in Desa Sri Hartamas, in the restaurant category.
Other winners were Sekolah Kebangsaan Tok Randok in Ajil, Hulu Terengganu, in the school category; Petronas Presint 18 in Putrajaya, in the petrol station category; Sunway Square Mall in Subang, in the shopping centre category; and the southbound Seremban Rest and Recreation (R&R) area along the North-South Expressway, operated by PLUS Malaysia Berhad, in the R&R category.
The winner in each category received RM20,000 in cash, a trophy and a certificate of recognition.
In addition, Nga said KPKT would introduce a new category at next year’s TOTYA for the Best Toilet at institutions of higher learning, universities and colleges, to encourage more educational institutions to prioritise toilet cleanliness and maintenance. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman, Singapore police smash cross-border prostitution ring using Malaysia as base
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Police have dismantled a cross-border prostitution syndicate that used Malaysia as an offshore operational command centre to market sex workers to clients in Singapore, arresting one local and 29 foreign nationals in a coordinated bilateral blitz.
The joint crackdown, dubbed Op Noda – Rentas Sempadan, was mounted on Oct 20 by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) alongside the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to stamp out networks managing online vice portals targeting Singaporean clientele.
“The success of this operation proves the effectiveness of the strategic synergy between the Royal Malaysia Police and the SPF through the sharing of intelligence, in achieving our common objective of curbing the activities of cross-border prostitution syndicates between both countries,” Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumarsaid in a statement today.
Equipped with intelligence on fugitives wanted across the Causeway, strike teams from Bukit Aman and the Johor contingent CID launched simultaneous raids on residential properties across Kuala Lumpur and Johor.
The opening wave of raids netted one Malaysian and eight foreign nationals, comprising five men and four women aged between 29 and 56. Checks on confiscated travel documents identified the foreign suspects as seven Chinese nationals and one Singaporean.
Investigators believe all nine operated as core members of a vice network wanted by the SPF under Section 146A(1)(b) of Singapore’s Women’s Charter 1961 and Section 109 of its Penal Code. Authorities also discovered that the Singaporean and four of the Chinese nationals were residing in Malaysia on expired visas.
Arrangements are underway to extradite the nine suspects to Singapore via Bukit Aman CID’s D12 division (Interpol/NCB) once their identities are confirmed before a magistrate under Section 5(3) of the Summons and Warrants (Special Provisions) Act 1971.
A concurrent phase of the operation netted another 21 foreign nationals, consisting of five men and 16 women aged 19 to 41, who are suspected of administering the syndicate’s online promotional machinery. The group includes 17 Chinese nationals, three Vietnamese, and one Laotian. Officers seized an array of electronic gadgets and communications gear allegedly used to field client queries and coordinate bookings.
The 21 suspects have been remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code. They face prosecution under Section 372(1)(e) of the Penal Code for exploiting individuals for prostitution through advertisements, an offence punishable by up to 15 years in prison, caning, and a fine.
They are also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering and remaining without a valid pass, which carries fines up to RM10,000, a maximum five-year jail term, and up to six strokes of the cane, alongside Section 15(1)(c) for overstaying.
Intelligence suggests the syndicate had operated in Singapore since 2024. By shifting its telecommunications hub and web hosting management to Malaysian residential hideouts, the syndicate sought to evade detection and complicate enforcement action by Singapore authorities.
Kumar warned that police will sustain “total enforcement” alongside local municipal authorities against all illicit vice networks, citing their destabilising toll on the economy and public welfare, and urged the community to continue tipping off law enforcement on cross-border syndicates.

Title: Health select committee taking haze concerns to Indonesian Embassy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Health (JKPK) will submit a memorandum regarding the cross-border haze issue to the Indonesian Embassy today.
Its chairman, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai), said that the haze issue poses problems for the country across various aspects, such as the environment, public health, citizen safety, the national economy, and diplomatic relations between neighbouring countries.
"God willing, tomorrow morning the JKPK and its members will submit a memorandum to the Indonesian Embassy regarding this haze issue," he said while taking part in the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Meanwhile, Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) urged the government to take firm action against local companies allegedly involved in forest fires in Indonesia that caused the cross-border haze.
He said this follows a recent Greenpeace report naming 20 companies believed to be involved, including a leading national plantation company through its subsidiary registered in the neighbouring country.
"KLCC has now become 'KL Cannot See' because of the haze. In previous Special Chamber debates, the ministry informed that there was no information regarding the involvement of local companies.
"However, through this Greenpeace report, it is proven that there are local subsidiaries involved. We hope the ministry will not sit idly by and will take serious follow-up steps," he said.
Therefore, Khoo suggested that Malaysia follow the firm action of the Singaporean government in issuing warning notices to 10 companies believed to have links to the forest fire incidents in Indonesia.
Vivian Wong Shir Yee (PH-Sandakan) urged the government to provide a specific allocation for the long-term implementation of the Trap-Neuter-Release (TNR) method to address the stray animal issue nationwide, thereby breaking the cycle of conflict between the public, local authorities (PBT), and animal lovers following capture operations.
"When we lack a long-term system, every capture operation risks becoming a conflict, whether between animal lovers and the authorities or neighbour against neighbour. In the end, no one wins. Animals suffer, personnel are criticised, and public trust is eroded," she said.
According to Wong, a continuous TNR programme can gradually and ethically reduce the stray animal population without having to wait for tragedies to repeat.
The issue of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) was also raised during the debate, with Rodiyah Sapiee (GPS-Batang Sadong) asking the government to provide comprehensive insurance protection, including death and permanent disability compensation, as well as the welfare of health personnel involved in the FDS.
"I welcome the increase in the FDS health service incentive from RM30 to RM100. However, taking into account the risks faced by health personnel in the interior as well as lessons learned from the recent FDS helicopter crash incident, the government must ensure comprehensive protection," she said.
Datuk Andi Muhammad Suryady Bandy (BN-Kalabakan) raised the issue that 36 per cent, or 382 out of 1,055 medical officers offered permanent placements in Sabah and Sarawak this year, failed to report for duty, and suggested that the government review the Regional Incentive Payment (BIW) rate, which is currently set at RM360 per month.
"The BIW should be reverted to a percentage-based calculation system of salary as before, or a reasonable minimum rate set for officers serving in the interior of Sabah and Sarawak.
"Additionally, a special quota of 30 percent for students from Sabah and Sarawak in medical fields at public universities should be established," he said.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: New MyKad security features, transboundary haze measures among topics in Dewan Rakyat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The justification for introducing a new-generation MyKad, its security levels, and cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia in tackling cross-border haze are among topics expected to take center stage during the Dewan Rakyat sitting today.
According to the Order Paper, during the question-and-answer session, Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) will ask the Minister of Home Affairs to explain the extent to which enhanced security features, chip technology, and identity verification systems on the new MyKad can combat forgery, cloning, and the misuse of citizens’ identities, while ensuring their personal data remains protected.
Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar) wants the Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability to explain the diplomatic actions and cooperation implemented by the Malaysian government with the Indonesian government to mitigate the risk of cross-border haze.
Also expected to draw attention is a question from Yeo Bee Yin (PH-Puchong) to the Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry regarding the latest status of the initiative to produce 60,000 skilled workers in the semiconductor field under the National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS), including the number of individuals trained and the budget spent so far.
Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) will ask the Minister of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives to state the percentage of micro-entrepreneurs who received financing and assistance from the ministry’s agencies from 2023 to 2026, those who successfully upgraded their business category to small or medium enterprises (SMEs), and the business failure rate after three years.
Additionally, Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) will pose a question to the Minister of Transport regarding the full implementation schedule of the open payment system for all public transportation services in the Klang Valley.
Following the question-and-answer session, the sitting is scheduled to proceed with the tabling of the Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons (Amendment) Bill 2026 for its first reading by the Minister of Home Affairs.
The sitting will then resume the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Minister of Finance, on October 9.
Based on the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 runs from October 12 to 22, prior to the winding-up sessions by relevant ministers for four days beginning October 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: New haj plan could cut waiting time to under 70 years, says minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The implementation of the Haj Preparation Plan, or
Seruan Istito’ah
, which replaces the previous haj waiting-list management process, has the potential to cut the waiting period by more than half to under 70 years, compared with about 150 years previously.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs)  Zulkifli Hasan said the current estimated waiting period provided by the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) could, however, change.
He said this would depend, among other factors, on the number of depositors who meet the stipulated minimum savings requirement, Malaysia’s official haj quota in the future, and current developments, particularly in the Holy Land.
“Beginning Jan 1, 2029, the haj waiting list will be systematically and automatically reorganised based on registration dates among those who have reached the minimum savings threshold of RM15,000.
“For those who have registered but have yet to reach the minimum amount, their places will be included in the active haj waiting list once they meet the savings readiness requirement,” he said in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat published on Parliament’s website today.
He was responding to a question from Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) on the actual waiting period for depositors who have reached the minimum savings threshold of RM15,000 to perform the haj, as well as the status of long-registered depositors whose savings remain insufficient.
Zulkifli said registered haj depositors would be given a transition period of more than two years, until Dec 31, 2028, to meet the minimum savings target of RM15,000. — Bernama

Title: Haze in Malaysia: 22 areas still at ‘Unhealthy’ air quality levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Haze continued to blanket much of the peninsula this morning, with 22 of the country’s 68 monitoring stations in the unhealthy range, according to the Department of Environment (DOE).
As of 8am, the DOE dashboard showed 22 stations with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of 101 to 200. Another 39 stations were in the moderate range and seven were in the good range. No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels.
The unhealthy count is down from 25 at 4pm yesterday, when 35 stations were moderate and eight were good.
Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded the highest reading at 174, up from 166 yesterday afternoon. It displaced Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur, which topped yesterday’s list at 173 but has since eased to 159. Bandaraya Melaka rose to 162 from 156, and Alor Gajah to 158 from 156, so all three Melaka stations remain unhealthy.
Negeri Sembilan’s readings were broadly steady. Nilai recorded 161, down from 165, Seremban 158, down from 161, and Port Dickson 155, up slightly from 154.
In Selangor, Johan Setia, near a peat fire hotspot, recorded 160, down from 171 yesterday. Klang and Banting were both at 159, Shah Alam at 158 and Petaling Jaya at 157, all lower than yesterday afternoon. In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras eased to 159 from 169, while Putrajaya recorded 158, down from 164.
Johor had seven unhealthy stations. Batu Pahat recorded 157, up from 153, and Larkin 155, down from 159. Tangkak stood at 153, Pasir Gudang at 152 and Kluang at 151. Segamat recorded 123, and Kota Tinggi fell sharply to 111 from 155 yesterday, the lowest reading on this morning’s unhealthy list. Pengerang, which was at 155 yesterday afternoon, is no longer in the unhealthy range.
Paka in Terengganu was the only station outside the west coast and Johor still unhealthy, at 153. The three Perak stations unhealthy yesterday, Tasek Ipoh, Pegoh Ipoh and Tanjung Malim, have dropped off the list.
Haze has persisted despite recent rainfall, which offered only temporary relief while fresh smoke continued to drift in from forest fires in Indonesia. Veterinarians have also reported pets suffering respiratory problems, including asthma attacks in cats and dogs needing oxygen therapy.
Authorities have previously advised high-risk groups and people with respiratory conditions to wear masks outdoors and to monitor hourly API updates on official DOE channels.

Title: PKR rejects Mukhriz claim linking party to PN deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has denied any involvement in the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the registration of Perikatan Nasional (PN) today.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh described as defamatory the allegation by Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang) president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir that the decision was made on PKR’s recommendation.
She also refuted Mukhriz’s social media post featuring several slides purportedly detailing PKR’s plan to deregister PN, which he claimed had been presented at the party’s 2026 National Congress in Melaka last August.
“I consider the use of slides that were never presented, in an attempt to link PKR to the RoS decision on PN, to be defamatory.
“I therefore demand that Mukhriz retract the allegation and apologise to PKR. Political differences are no licence to spread defamatory allegations,” she said in a Facebook post.
Fuziah added that the complaint which prompted the RoS action against PN concerned issues involving the coalition’s own component parties, and PKR had absolutely no involvement in the matter.
In a statement today, RoS said it deregistered PN after finding that the explanation submitted by the coalition had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.
RoS said it made the decision after examining all the documents and explanations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
It added that the reasons provided by PN also failed to offer sufficient justification for maintaining the coalition’s registration. — Bernama

Title: Penang ramps up efforts to tackle Parit Cina, Sungai Kereh pollution
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 21 — Clean-up works at Parit Cina and Sungai Kereh in Tasek Gelugor are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 to remove accumulated sediment, improve water flow and help reduce pollution in the area.
State Local Government and Town & Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the initiative was among the state government’s efforts to address the pollution of Sungai Kereh, an issue that has persisted for decades.
He said 61 pig farms are currently operating in Kampung Selamat, Tasek Gelugor, but the source of the pollution has to be identified based on evidence and on-site inspection findings, rather than drawing conclusions based on a single activity.
“The pollution issue in Kampung Selamat needs to be examined by taking into account various factors, including agricultural activities, waste management and discharge, drainage systems, and other environmental aspects that fall under the jurisdiction of various agencies.
“The state government’s priority for now is to ensure that the source of pollution in Sungai Kereh is identified through comprehensive inspections and assessments. Enforcement action will be taken against parties that violate regulations, and corrective measures will be implemented effectively,” he said in a statement today.
H’ng said the state government is also strengthening pig farm waste management through a short-term action plan involving the transportation of waste to biogas plants, and a long-term plan involving a proposal to construct a biogas plant facility in Kampung Selamat, as presented by the Penang Veterinary Services Department on May 11.
Under the short-term plan, he said solid and liquid waste from pig farms in Kampung Selamat is being transported to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar.
For pig farms in Seberang Perai Tengah, the transportation of solid and liquid waste to the biogas plant in Kampung Valdor began in June 2026, while waste transportation from farms in Seberang Perai Selatan has commenced since 2023.
“These measures are aimed at strengthening livestock waste management through appropriate processing facilities and reducing the risk of waste discharge that could harm the environment.
“As for the long-term solution, a proposal to build a biogas plant facility in Kampung Selamat has also been put forward to enable livestock waste to be managed more systematically and sustainably,” he said.
H’ng said the pig farming industry has the potential to contribute to the state’s economic growth and support related sectors. However, this has to be balanced with operators’ responsibility to comply with regulations and ensure that farming activities do not adversely affect the environment or the well-being of the community.
Yesterday, Tasek Gelugor Member of Parliament Datuk Wan Saifulruddin Wan Jan proposed in the Dewan Rakyat that pig farming activities in Tasek Gelugor be halted following the pollution of Sungai Kereh, which has been linked to the discharge of untreated waste from nearby pig farms in Kampung Selamat. — Bernama

Title: Border agency chief Shuhaily in court over alleged KLIA assault of two Special Branch cops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia Checkpoints and Border Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain arrived at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court this morning to face two charges of assault linked to an altercation with two Special Branch officers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Security was tight across the court grounds, with an augmented contingent of police and Rela personnel restricting compound vehicle access strictly to authorised court staff and law enforcement officers,
NST
reported.
Dressed in a dark suit, the 54-year-old border agency chief appeared calm and composed upon his arrival. He made a stop at the court cafeteria for breakfast ahead of the proceedings, warmly extending an invitation to waiting press photographers and reporters to join him.
Lending a show of solidarity at the court complex was Port Klang MCBA commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
Shuhaily is set to face two counts of voluntarily causing hurt under Section 323 of the Penal Code for allegedly striking Lance Corporals Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman.
If convicted, the offence is punishable by a prison term of up to one year, a maximum fine of RM2,000, or both. Criminal defence lawyer Kitson Foong is appearing for Shuhaily.
The charges stem from a high-profile confrontation at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28, which thrust the agency into the spotlight after mobile footage went viral online. The clip appeared to capture a senior official matching Shuhaily’s likeness berating two men at the terminal, with one of the officers seemingly grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Following the viral uproar, Shuhaily publicly said on Oct 1 that he was prepared to bear full responsibility and accept whatever determination the government reached regarding the episode.
The case progressed to court following an intensive review between investigators and the prosecution. Police initially recorded statements from 25 witnesses before submitting the investigation papers to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC).
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar returned the dossier on Oct 8 for supplementary work, leading Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail to confirm on Oct 17 that prosecutors had demanded further clarification before framing charges.
The legal fallout widened on Oct 12 when Faiz lodged a follow-up police report through his lawyers, Kamal Hisham Ja’afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin. The report claimed new evidence, alleging that his smartphone was confiscated while he attempted to photograph the airport dispute.
The two Special Branch personnel, deployed as travel control officers at the international gateway, have strenuously rejected suggestions that they were touting or facilitating “counter setting” syndicates to bypass immigration controls.

Title: Government open to KWAP, EPF RCI subject to findings, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 —The government is open to considering a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), should the need arise.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said this would apply if there is concrete information, evidence, or findings indicating a necessity for a comprehensive and independent public inquiry.
She added that the government remains committed to ensuring that any issues concerning the management of public funds including aspects of governance and investment decisions are examined based on facts and evidence, through appropriate oversight mechanisms.
“If the findings indicate a clear public need and interest for a special inquiry, a proposal to establish a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) may be duly considered.
“In determining the necessity for an RCI whether it concerns institutions that manage public funds or any other institution the government takes into account public interest, the gravity of the issue, as well as available facts and evidence,” she said in a written reply to the Dewan Rakyat, which was published on the Parliament’s website today.
Azalina made these remarks in response to a question from Datuk Seri Dr. Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) regarding whether the government is prepared to consider establishing an RCI concerning KWAP (Retirement Fund Incorporated) and the EPF (Employees Provident Fund) in relation to their governance, investment management, or questionable financial decisions.
Addressing Shahidan’s query on the criteria used to determine the need for an RCI into institutions that manage public funds, Azalina explained that the prevailing Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) require such a proposal to be submitted via a Cabinet Memorandum by the lead ministry.
“The memorandum is then submitted for Cabinet approval. Once approved, the Prime Minister will present the proposal to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to seek His Majesty’s consent.
“If consent is granted, the establishment of the RCI will involve defining its terms of reference, membership, and the duration of the inquiry. These details are subsequently finalised through a gazette notification in the Federal Government Gazette before the RCI commences its functions,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Why won’t the rain wash away Malaysia’s haze? Experts explain what’s keeping the smoke coming
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia, particularly the Klang Valley, has been experiencing bouts of heavy rain and thunderstorms in recent days, but the haze continues to linger. Why?
According to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, rainfall can provide only temporary relief as long as smoke continues to arrive from Indonesia.
“The haze currently affecting the country is caused by transboundary haze, whereby smoke from fire-affected areas in neighbouring countries is carried into Malaysian airspace.
“At the same time, the country is experiencing the monsoon transition phase, characterised by weak winds blowing from various directions.
“These conditions are conducive to the formation of rain clouds and thunderstorms in the afternoon and early evening.
“Rainfall during the monsoon transition can only temporarily reduce haze conditions. Therefore, haze may persist despite rainfall if smoke continues to be carried in by winds from other areas,” he told
Malay Mail
.
Universiti Malaya meteorologist Professor Datuk Azizan Abu Samah said the prevailing wind direction was a key reason the haze could persist even after rainfall.
As long as winds continued to blow from the south, south-west or west, smoke from Indonesia would continue to be carried into Malaysia, he explained.
“So even if the rain cleared due to wet deposition, new smoke will be blown back from Sumatra,” he said.
According to deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas, fires in Indonesia burned more than 1.9 million hectares between January and the end of September this year, an area nearly 12 times the size of London.
Forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, particularly in Sumatra and Kalimantan, have been blamed for much of the haze affecting Malaysia, with smoke carried across borders by prevailing winds.
The haze has disrupted daily life in Malaysia in recent weeks, with worsening air quality prompting health concerns and school closures.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said Malaysia remains prepared to extend assistance to Indonesia in tackling the forest and land fires responsible for the transboundary haze.
Mohd Hisham explained that heavy, prolonged rainfall over a wide area could remove more pollutant particles from the atmosphere than brief, localised drizzle, although its effectiveness also depended on the size and properties of the particles and atmospheric conditions.
“A greater volume of rainwater and a longer duration of rainfall can enhance the removal of pollutant particles. However, the effectiveness of rainfall is also influenced by the size and properties of pollutant particles, as well as atmospheric conditions.
“Heavy rain does not necessarily guarantee that haze will clear completely if smoke continues to be carried into Malaysia from fire-affected areas in neighbouring countries.
“In the context of transboundary haze, changes in wind direction that reduce the transport of smoke into Malaysia, together with sufficient and sustained rainfall in affected areas, are crucial to improving air quality,” he said.
Explaining why the haze could return after rain, Mohd Hisham said smoke from forest and land fires typically contained fine suspended particles such as PM2.5 and PM10, including black carbon and organic carbon produced by burning organic matter.
PM2.5 particles are particularly fine and can remain suspended in the air for long periods, allowing them to travel considerable distances with the wind.
Certain gases released during combustion can also react in the atmosphere to form secondary pollutant particles, he said.
“Rain can remove some of these particles, but not all particles are necessarily removed at the same rate. When fresh smoke continues to enter Malaysia due to winds from fire-affected areas, pollutant concentrations can remain high or rise again,” Mohd Hisham said.
Azizan said the scale of the forest and peatland fires in Sumatra meant there was little technology could do to resolve the haze quickly.
“The scale of the environmental disaster is too big for a technological fix,” he said, adding that rainfall in Sumatra during October and November could help extinguish the fires.
Mohd Hisham also warned that hot and dry conditions could increase the risk of forest and land fires, particularly in areas with dry vegetation and peat soil.
“Ongoing fires will release more smoke and pollutant particles into the atmosphere, making it more difficult to reduce haze.
“The presence of a very strong Super El Niño phenomenon will further worsen weather conditions in the region and increase the risk of transboundary haze, such as the situation currently being experienced,” he said.
But a change in the weather could finally offer Malaysians some relief.
Mohd Hisham said the haze was expected to gradually subside next week following an anticipated change in wind direction.
During the Northeast Monsoon, stronger north-easterly winds and more widespread rainfall were expected to help improve air quality, he said.
Azizan said Malaysia would have to wait for the Northeast Monsoon to bring a more lasting improvement, with easterly and north-easterly winds expected to carry smoke away from the country.
He said the north-easterly wind belt was already present over the South China Sea near Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and was expected to reach Peninsular Malaysia in early November.
“We just need to stay safe and let nature take its course,” he said, estimating that the country would have to endure the conditions for another two to three weeks.

Title: Haze is making pets sick too: Malaysian vets report cats suffering asthma attacks, dogs needing oxygen therapy
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — Haze and poor air quality are taking a toll on pets, with veterinarians reporting respiratory problems in cats, birds and dogs, including cases requiring oxygen therapy, as polluted air continues to affect parts of Malaysia.
Dr Wendy Cheng of Noah’s Ark Veterinary Clinic said fine particles in polluted air, including PM2.5, could irritate animals’ respiratory systems and aggravate existing heart or lung conditions.
She said she had personally seen cats experiencing asthma attacks and birds breathing with their mouths open, while a puppy had recently required oxygen therapy and nebulisation at a clinic.
“Symptoms owners should watch for include sneezing, coughing, nasal discharge, watery or irritated eyes, wheezing, rapid breathing, reduced appetite and unusual lethargy,” she said.
Open-mouth breathing, particularly in cats, or obvious difficulty breathing should be treated as an emergency, she added.
Veterinarian Dr Wendy Cheng of Noah’s Ark with a parrot. She urged pet owners to watch for signs of respiratory distress during the haze, particularly in animals with existing health conditions. — Picture courtesy of Dr Wendy Cheng
Meanwhile, Sabah-based veterinarian Dr Randolf Paza, who has 37,000 followers on Facebook and runs the Dr Haiwan Sabah Instagram account, said veterinary clinics and animal shelters in Peninsular Malaysia had also encountered animals experiencing respiratory problems amid unhealthy air quality.
“According to my peers, there are several cases where pets have been brought to clinics with symptoms that look like choking, but are actually coughing,” he said.
“The pets were given oxygen therapy, and some got better while others continued to show symptoms.”
Dr Paza also warned of the dangers of prolonged exposure to smoke and fine airborne particles.
“The haze from fires is dangerous because of the tiny particles that can affect the lungs and remain there, making it difficult to breathe,” he said.
He added that prolonged exposure, if left untreated, could also affect animals' appetite and potentially lead to more serious health complications.
With air quality remaining a concern, Dr Cheng advised owners to keep pets indoors as much as possible and limit outdoor walks and strenuous activities.
She also recommended keeping windows closed, using an air purifier with a high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filter where available, and ensuring pets have access to fresh drinking water.
“Owners should also avoid exposing pets to cigarette smoke, incense, scented candles and aerosol sprays indoors. Senior animals, flat-faced breeds and pets with existing heart or respiratory conditions require closer monitoring,” she said.
Veterinarian Dr Randolf Paza examines a puppy. He warned that haze and fine airborne particles could cause breathing difficulties in animals, sometimes requiring oxygen therapy. — Picture courtesy of Dr Randolf Paza
Dr Paza similarly urged pet owners to monitor air quality and their animals’ condition without panicking, and to reassess precautions as conditions changed.
The warnings come as Malaysia continues to grapple with haze linked to forest and peatland fires in Indonesia, with smoke affecting air quality across parts of the country.
As of 9am on October 19, 27 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, according to the Department of Environment's air-quality monitoring system, as reported by Bernama.
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading at 172, while seven areas in Johor, including Tangkak, Pasir Gudang and Batu Pahat, also registered unhealthy air quality.
Other affected areas included parts of Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Pahang and Sarawak. API readings between 101 and 200 are classified as unhealthy.
For animals experiencing severe respiratory distress, veterinary clinics may administer oxygen therapy through oxygen delivery devices or oxygen chambers.
In severe cases, prolonged exposure to polluted air can lead to life-threatening respiratory complications, making early intervention particularly important.
“Pet owners should seek veterinary attention promptly if their animals show signs of breathing difficulties, particularly if symptoms worsen or do not improve,” Dr Cheng said.

Title: Haze: Schools remain open in six states, KL and Putrajaya tomorrow, outdoor activities halted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) would operate as usual. However, the Final Academic Session Exam (UASA) scheduled during this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools.
The postponement also applies to all internal school examinations, in line with the MOE’s statement dated October 15. All outdoor activities must be suspended if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100.
In MELAKA, SELANGOR, PUTRAJAYA and KUALA LUMPUR, school administrators were instructed to monitor API readings issued by the Department of Environment and pay particular attention to pupils at higher risk.
In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.
Schools in other districts would operate as usual, with any changes to be announced through the respective District Education Offices.
The PERAK Education Department urged everyone to remain alert to developments and heed the authorities’ advice on the haze.
In PENANG, the state Education Department encouraged pupils to drink sufficient water and instructed schools to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
Pupils and school staff are also encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
The education departments in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, have also given parents and guardians who are concerned about their children’s health the option of keeping them at home, provided they inform the school.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said that decisions on school closures due to the haze were made jointly by the MOE, the Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on the expertise of each ministry.
She said the decisions took into account air quality monitoring and the health risks to pupils, as well as the impact on learning if schools remained closed for too long.
Meanwhile, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
Her Majesty stressed the importance of community cooperation to strengthen the effectiveness of home-based teaching and learning (PdPR), as well as developing long-term strategies to deal with the haze. — Bernama

Title: From Waze to TuJu? Anwar backs Malaysian navigation app over data security concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is encouraging the public to use the locally developed application, TuJu created by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) as an alternative for road navigation needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this alternative has been proposed due to security risks concerning information and data on citizens’ movements, given that the Waze application is subject to the laws of the Israeli government.
He noted that this matter was among the topics discussed while chairing the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) today, which aimed to examine evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation’s preparedness and digital sovereignty.
“Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).
“We cannot compromise when it comes to the security of our citizens’ data and identities. Therefore, the government is strengthening an integrated identity ecosystem utilising MyKad as a physical credential and MyDigital ID for digital transactions supported by more robust cyber protections, including preparations for future threats via PQC,” he said in a Facebook post.
The prime minister emphasised that these efforts are crucial to ensuring that the digitalization of public services continues to benefit the people, without compromising security, public trust, or national sovereignty. — Bernama

Title: No action against UM student over viral ‘tough’ question, says Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a “tough” question during the i-Future programme.
Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students’ right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media.
“My position is clear. Respect students’ right to speak up. As we have stated, amendments to the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) have provided them with the space to express their views.
“This freedom should also be exercised responsibly, courteously and based on facts,” he said in a statement shared on TikTok today.
Earlier, a video lasting more than two minutes went viral, showing a Universiti Malaya Students’ Union representative firmly questioning a panel during a dialogue session held as part of the i-Future programme.
The student, among other things, expressed concerns about the integrity of leadership and criticised the collection of public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine imposed as one of the conditions for allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence for the SRC International case under house arrest.
Commenting on allegations of threats, abuse and condemnation directed at the student, Zambry said such behaviour should not occur and advised the student to lodge a police report to enable an investigation.
He urged the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to examine the posts and accounts involved, including the possibility that fake accounts had been used.
“If anyone has attempted to engage in wrongdoing, the student concerned should take appropriate action by lodging a report with the relevant authorities,” he said.
Zambry urged all parties not to politicise the issue or exploit students to advance specific agendas.
“I also urge everyone not to turn students into weapons of political propaganda, to the extent that they become victims of certain agendas.
“For example, some ministers have even called for shirts, T-shirts and the like to be made, whereas at the MOHE level, we have absolutely no intention of taking any action against the student concerned,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No driving licences without tests: JPJ warns against fake TikTok promotions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has denied the authenticity of a TikTok advertisement offering driving licences without the need to take a test.
In a statement today, JPJ said it received complaints regarding the advertisement, which used an account under the name ‘Ahmad Mushidi’.
“JPJ wishes to emphasise that the advertisement and the account belonging to the individual named Ahmad Mushidi are fake,” the statement read.
Following this, JPJ lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for further action.
JPJ advised the public not to be easily deceived by driving licence promotions through unverified advertisements or accounts to avoid confusion and losses.
The public is also reminded to obtain information regarding JPJ services only through the department’s official platforms. — Bernama

Title: Kampar woman loses over RM129,000 in online job scam
Article:
IPOH, Oct 20 — A local woman suffered losses of more than RM129,000 after being duped by a non-existent online part-time job offer.
Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim.
“Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. Interested, the victim left her phone number to be contacted by the party offering the job.
“The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job. The victim was then added to a WhatsApp group supposedly for handling online hotel booking transactions,” he said in a statement today.
Mohamad Nazri said the victim was instructed to make payments for each hotel booking into several bank accounts provided by the suspect, who promised that the capital would be returned along with a commission ranging between 10 to 20 percent, which would increase according to the transaction amount.
He said that due to being lured by the offer and the promise of profits, the victim carried out several money transfer transactions to eight accounts provided by the suspect.
“The victim began to realise she had been cheated when the promised capital and commission were not received after the payments were made. The victim suffered a loss of RM129,975.54,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis record highest drug abuse rates
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 individuals per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646).
“The ranking of these four states reflects the extent of drug addiction and abuse that requires attention and targeted intervention.
“Geographical factors also contribute to this situation, with cross-border smuggling routes identified as among the risk factors influencing drug-related problems in these areas,” he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.
He said the statistics were compiled based on integrated data from four main sources, namely Nada, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Health Ministry and private rehabilitation centres.
In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments: educational institutions, families and communities.
“A total of 242 prevention and public awareness programmes were conducted, involving 16,408 participants overall, including 228 programmes in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah, which involved more than 16,000 participants,” he said.
He added that 4,253 enforcement operations had been conducted nationwide, with 30,157 individuals detained for treatment and rehabilitation programmes as of last Sunday.
On treatment and rehabilitation, Ruslin said Nada prioritised a voluntary approach, with the average number of individuals seeking treatment on their own initiative rising from 75 a month in 2025 to 232 a month this year.
“This increase reflects positive progress following the implementation of amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into force on Aug 22, 2025,” he said.
He said Nada would continue to adopt a data-driven approach and strengthen cooperation with state governments through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD) meetings to coordinate prevention, treatment and rehabilitation efforts involving various agencies, families, educational institutions and communities.

Title: Selangor Education Department cooperating with probe into schoolgirl’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 20 — The Selangor State Education Department (JPN Selangor) will fully cooperate with the authorities’ investigations into the death of a Year One pupil after she experienced breathing difficulties at a school in Sepang.
In a statement today, JPN Selangor said the girl was reported to have had breathing difficulties at school and was taken to hospital for treatment.
“JPN Selangor extends its condolences and deepest sympathies to the pupil’s family. The department will ensure that the family’s welfare is given due attention, including assistance and psychosocial support as needed,” it said.
JPN Selangor will also ensure that due attention is given to the welfare and wellbeing of the school community affected by the incident.
“The public is advised not to speculate or spread unverified information regarding the incident. All parties are urged to respect the family’s privacy and give the authorities room to carry out their investigation,” the statement read.
Earlier, police confirmed that a seven-year-old girl died after she was believed to have experienced breathing difficulties while in class in Dengkil yesterday.
Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report on the incident at 7.30 pm yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Police record statements over podcast video on alleged drug trafficking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here.
Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
He said the investigation was initiated following a police report lodged by the chairman of the Marathadi Madurai Veeran Temple in Kuala Lumpur last Sunday to strongly deny the allegations made in the video.
“After receiving the Order to Investigate (OTI) from the Deputy Public Prosecutor, police have called several witnesses to assist in completing the investigation,” he said in a statement today.
He said the podcast guest, Azrul Affandi Sobry, will appear at the Sentul IPD at noon tomorrow to have his statement recorded.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus was previously reported as saying that the allegations raised in the video posted on the @Sembangohhyeahh TikTok account actually referred to an incident that occurred 10 years ago.
He said checks found that the incident took place on July 12, 2016, and that the podcast content was merely a retelling of the guest’s experience while monitoring the situation as a journalist at the time.
Fadil also stressed that such publicity was inappropriate as it could create negative public perceptions of the level of integrity of police, and advised all parties to be more responsible when disseminating information. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution urges Asean to translate anti-crime pledges into results
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks.
He noted that the threat of transnational crime has become increasingly complex due to the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), necessitating a faster and more integrated response from Asean member states.
"Asean’s success cannot be measured solely by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the criminal networks dismantled, the victims protected, and the criminals brought to justice.
"This is the commitment that Malaysia is bringing to Manila. Regional cooperation must yield tangible benefits for the security of the people, rather than remaining merely as commitments on paper," he said when delivering the National Statement at the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC) in Manila, Philippines, today.
Saifuddin Nasution noted that Malaysia has outlined three priorities to strengthen Asean cooperation: accelerating cross-border responses to online fraud and illicit financial flows; enhancing investigative capabilities including the handling of digital evidence and asset recovery; and improving operational collaboration between member states and international partners.
He emphasised that the need to expedite such cooperation has become increasingly urgent, given that proceeds of crime can be moved across borders in a matter of minutes, whereas investigative and legal processes typically take much longer.
Consequently, he argued that regional cooperation mechanisms must prioritise the detection of illicit funds, the preservation of digital evidence, and the coordination of investigations to ensure that criminal syndicates cannot exploit gaps in law enforcement between nations.
Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026-2035) and the Melaka Declaration.
He added that the continuity of these efforts is further reinforced by the Work Programme of the Asean Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) for 2026-2028, which was adopted last June.
"Currently, our primary challenge is to ensure that all frameworks for cooperation has resulted in tangible actions and outcomes," he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia will continue to play an active role as an Asean voluntary lead country in the areas of money laundering and human trafficking, with the aim of strengthening information exchange, capacity building, and enforcement cooperation among member states.
He noted that Malaysia also hosted the inaugural meeting of the Asean Working Group on Money Laundering in Kuala Lumpur last April, as part of efforts to enhance the coordination of regional actions.
Saifuddin Nasution also shared the measures implemented by Malaysia to address transnational crime, including the establishment of the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) which operates 24 hours a day and can be reached via the 997 hotline since March.
Furthermore, he mentioned that Malaysia has strengthened its cyber-legal framework through the passing of the Cybercrime Bill 2026 in July, and has enhanced border controls by empowering the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency.
He added that efforts to combat terrorism and violent extremism are also being pursued through the Malaysia Action Plan on Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (MyPCVE) 2024-2028, which focuses on prevention, enforcement, rehabilitation, and reintegration. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi calls for stronger Asean cooperation on child online safety
Article:
BALI, Oct 20 — Asean countries must work together to protect children from growing online threats despite differences in their laws and approaches to internet safety, said Malaysia’s Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said countries in the region shared the challenge of keeping the internet safe for children and needed to strengthen cooperation to address these threats.
“The internet is good. The internet can be put to good use. But do children know how to use it well?” he said in his keynote address at Bali Tech Week 2026, initiated by Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Digital today.
Fahmi said Malaysia wanted to ensure that children below the age of 16 were unable to open social media accounts, although approaches to online safety for children could differ between Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and other Asean countries.
Malaysia began enforcing age-verification requirements for social media account registration on June 1 this year under the Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code introduced under the Online Safety Act 2025.
Under the new regulations, individuals under the age of 16 are no longer allowed to open any social media accounts, while those who wish to register must submit official identification documents such as MyKad, passport or MyDigital ID to verify their age.
Fahmi also highlighted the challenges posed by social media algorithms, noting that governments had limited understanding of how they operated and influenced the content users encountered.
At the forum, Fahmi outlined Malaysia’s efforts to improve internet coverage, speed and affordability while making online access safer, particularly for children.
Highlighting the dangers children faced online, he cited a recent case in which Malaysian police apprehended 53 suspected paedophiles and seized more than half a million files suspected of containing child sexual abuse material.
He described online child protection as a challenge faced by countries across the region.
Fahmi also said that governments needed to consider how they shaped people’s choices while ensuring individuals had the freedom to make more informed decisions.
Bali Tech Week, themed “Archipelago Ascending: Advance Together, Innovate Further”, is being held from Oct 19 to 23 at the Bali Beach Convention Centre in Sanur, bringing together policymakers, technology leaders, innovators and investors.
Fahmi was invited by his Indonesian counterpart, Meutya Hafid, to deliver the keynote address at the event during his working visit to Indonesia from Monday to Thursday.
He will travel to Jakarta later Tuesday to continue his official engagements. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin saddened by Perikatan deregistration, warns against abuse of power in coalitions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed sadness over the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN), describing the development as a lesson for leaders of political coalitions to act fairly towards all member parties and comply with their constitutions and the law.
In a statement, Muhyiddin, who founded PN, said he was saddened by the coalition's deregistration.
"However, this decision is a reminder to any party leading a coalition to act fairly towards all member parties and to always comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966," he said.
Muhyiddin also cautioned against the misuse of power and position within a political coalition for the benefit of a particular party or group.
He said such actions could cause a coalition to drift away from the original objectives and purpose behind its formation.
"Do not misuse power and position in a coalition solely for the interests of a particular party or group to the point where the coalition deviates from its original goals and objectives," he said.
Muhyiddin added that he would discuss the way forward with the Bersatu leadership at a special Political Bureau meeting scheduled for tonight.
Earlier today, the Registrar of Societies announced the deregistration of PN after finding that the coalition's explanation had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.

Title: Selangor Sultan cautions royal family members against exploiting royal status
Article:
KLANG, Oct 20 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain.
His Royal Highness stressed that royal status did not give anyone the right to act as they pleased, reminding family members to respect the law and comply with all regulations.
“We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. Every family member is accountable for their conduct and actions, as the behaviour of one individual can affect public perceptions of the entire royal family.
“The way we conduct ourselves, interact with society and fulfil our responsibilities must reflect the dignity and integrity of the royal family and institution,” His Royal Highness said at a royal tea reception with members of the royal family in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign at Padang Mahkota, Istana Alam Shah, here today.
Also present were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah and his wife, Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz.
The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.
His Royal Highness said differences of opinion and misunderstandings should be resolved wisely and amicably, without spreading false stories, provoking disputes or making hurtful remarks.
“Be mindful of your words and manners, including when using social media, and practise mutual understanding, tolerance and forgiveness.
“I also urge family members to support and care for one another. We should not gather only for ceremonies and celebrations but also offer help and support when our relatives face difficulties,” the Sultan said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also called for the values of compassion, responsibility and mutual respect between older and younger generations to be nurtured and passed down to future generations.
At the same time, the Sultan also expressed delight at the attendance of nearly 1,200 members of the Selangor royal family, saying the Silver Jubilee celebration provided a meaningful opportunity to strengthen family ties.
“Some of my relatives who are here this afternoon are people I have not seen for a long time, while others belong to the younger generation who have now reached adulthood. Your presence means a great deal to me.
“This gathering not only brings me joy but also reminds us of our shared responsibility to preserve family harmony and the dignity of the Selangor royal institution,” His Royal Highness said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar backs efforts to strengthen IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed efforts to strengthen the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, positioning it as a hub for the sharing of knowledge and expertise.
He noted that Malaysia is recognised for its experience in empowering micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening economic resilience, and generating employment opportunities, expertise and experience that could potentially benefit other IsDB member countries.
“I also emphasised Malaysia’s readiness to share its expertise and expand development cooperation at the international level,” he said in a post on X today.
He mentioned that this was discussed during a meeting today with IsDB president Dr. Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, reflecting a continued confidence in the nation’s development trajectory and governance.
“God willing, this close collaboration will further enhance Malaysia’s role as a credible development partner, while bringing the expertise of our people to the global stage,” he added.
The IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, launched in 2019, serves as a strategic platform for the transfer of technology, expertise, and best practices in Islamic finance from Malaysia to the 56 other IsDB member countries.
The IsDB, headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, is a multilateral development finance institution established in 1975 to support the economic development and social progress of its member countries and Muslim communities worldwide, based on Shariah principles. — Bernama
